# Decisions

Architectural / process decisions. Never deleted — strikethrough if reversed.

## 2026-08-22 — TASK-253 recover a replay stranded by a host crash mid-flight

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-22 | Recovery **FAILS** the stranded row (`executed` → `failed`, releasing its partial-unique-index slot). It never retries the call. | We cannot know which side of the tool's own side effect the crash landed on — the executor may have returned microseconds before the process died, or its HTTP request may have landed with the response never arriving. Retrying is therefore a coin-flip on a double send, which on this surface is strictly worse than the bug being fixed. The corollary is the actual safety property: because the reclaim runs NOTHING, reclaiming a still-live flight cannot execute anything twice — the worst it can do is release an authorisation, and a human still has to approve the same call again before a second one goes out. `markReplayed` is unconditional on status, so a late-returning executor even writes the truth back over the reclaim. | (a) Re-run the call — REJECTED, double-send risk. (b) `restore` to `pending` — REJECTED, erases the fact the person answered and re-offers the card as an unanswered question. (c) Clear only `replay_claimed_at` and leave it `executed` — REJECTED, does not free the index slot, so the card's actual bug survives. |
| 2026-08-22 | The age cutoff is `STRANDED_REPLAY_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 min`, derived rather than felt. | A host replay is one `bus.call('tool:execute:<name>')`, and `HookBus` wraps every service call in `DEFAULT_SERVICE_TIMEOUT_MS` = **120 s** (nothing in the repo overrides it for a tool executor, and no host overrides `defaultServiceTimeoutMs`). So a live flight cannot outlast ~120 s in ANY replica — they all run the same ceiling. 15 min is that bound plus an order of magnitude, which is where cross-host clock skew on `replay_claimed_at` goes. Erring LONG is the safe direction because the cutoff is not the safety property (see above); a tight cutoff would cancel yeses that were about to be honoured. | A lease/heartbeat — REJECTED, a second liveness store for a fact the row already implies (invariant 4) and far more machinery than a sweep that runs nothing. |
| 2026-08-22 | It lives in the existing **`decisions:sweep`** (a new `reclaimed` count on its output), ordered BEFORE the due-replay pass. | `decisions:sweep` is already registered as a hook AND run on a timer specifically so a test or operator can drive maintenance deterministically; a second mechanism would be a second answer to "what runs on a timer". Ordering first means a slot released this pass is already free for anything later in it — free, since the reclaim runs no calls and so cannot reorder an outward action. | A new `decisions:reclaim` hook — REJECTED, no caller wants it separately and the boundary cost buys nothing. |
| 2026-08-22 | New nullable column + `Decision` field **`replayAbandonedAt`**, and a distinct receipt sentence `ABANDONED_RECEIPT`. NOT a new `DecisionStatus`. | `FAILED_RECEIPT` ends "Nothing was completed" — a REPORT, true when the executor threw. On an abandoned row it is a claim we have no standing to make, and the expensive direction of the H1 lie: a person who believes it goes and redoes an irreversible action. The row could not otherwise tell the two apart — every `failed` row carries `replay_claimed_at` set and `replayed_at` null, because a replay that threw was in flight too. A new status would ripple into channel-web's `workspace-types.ts`, `decision-copy.ts`, `DecisionRow.tsx` and the routes for a case with no different rendering; `DecisionReceiptOutcome` stays `failed` and only the sentence differs. | (a) Reuse `FAILED_RECEIPT` — REJECTED, false. (b) Infer "abandoned" from `failed` + cleared `replay_claimed_at` — REJECTED, an implicit invariant a future `markFailed` edit silently flips. (c) Key the receipt off `replayError` text — REJECTED, receipts derived by string surgery is exactly what `templates.ts` forbids. (d) New status `abandoned` — REJECTED, cross-package ripple for no renderer difference. |
| 2026-08-22 | (review F1) The refusal sentence is **gated on the cause**: `claimForApproval` translates a pg `23505` into a typed `DuplicateAuthorisationError` and lets every other write failure through untranslated; the handler rethrows anything that is not that type. The classification lives in the **store**, not the plugin. | The first cut answered "an identical request is already approved" for anything the claim threw while the comment asserted the cause as certain — the epic's signature defect in our own uniform. Under eviction/failover/load the same UPDATE throws a SELF-CLEARING `40P01` / `lock_timeout` / `statement_timeout` that is gone by the time `settle(null)` re-reads, so the person is told their approval was not recorded because an identical one is pending — and retry, the correct recovery, is exactly what that sentence talks them out of. A hard outage was safe only by luck (`settle`'s `get` also throws → 500). Store-side classification because `err.code === '23505'` in `plugin.ts` leaks Postgres into the plugin layer (invariant 1) and silently makes every alternate `DecisionStore` impl responsible for reproducing a SQLSTATE. | (a) Sniff `err.code` in the plugin — REJECTED, storage vocabulary above the store. (b) Also match the constraint NAME — REJECTED, no other unique index is reachable by that UPDATE (the PK is never rewritten), and an absent `.constraint` would 500 a benign double-approve. |
| 2026-08-22 | (review F2) `markReplayed` clears `replay_abandoned_at`. | A frozen host that thaws after the sweep gave up on it lands this write (unconditional on status, so the world wins) and produced an `executed` row still carrying a "we gave up on this" marker — harmless to `receiptFor`, which keys on `failed`, but a straight contradiction of the field's own doc comment. Chose to fix the CODE rather than soften the doc: same rule as the `replay_due_at`/`replay_error` clears two lines above, and it keeps "set ⟹ we gave up" absolute. | Soften the doc to admit the race — REJECTED, weakens an invariant that costs one line to actually hold. |
| 2026-08-22 | `decisions:approve` now returns a non-null `error` (`CLAIM_REFUSED_DETAIL`) when the partial unique index refuses the claim, instead of absorbing it silently. | Separate acceptance bullet: "re-approving a stranded call either succeeds or fails loudly — never a silent no-op". Absorbing the unique violation was right (it is not a 500) but doing it with `error: null` and an unchanged `pending` row is a button that does nothing and says nothing. Sweep owns recovery; approve owns loudness. | (a) Throw a `PluginError` — REJECTED, turns the benign double-approve into a 500. (b) Read the blocking row to say WHICH one — REJECTED, that row is keyed on `(agent, fingerprint)` not on the owner, so on a team agent it can belong to somebody else. (c) Reclaim inline and retry the claim — REJECTED as gold-plating: the sweep interval is 5 s, so the loud window is seconds, and a retry path in that handler is real complexity. |
| 2026-08-22 | Boundary review answered (two hook-surface changes: `decisions:sweep` output gains `reclaimed`, `Decision` gains `replayAbandonedAt`). | Alternate impl: any non-Postgres decisions store — the reclaim is `UPDATE ... WHERE` semantics, expressible anywhere. Leaky names: none (`reclaimed`, `replayAbandonedAt` are domain vocabulary; no `sha`/`bucket`/`pod_name`). Subscriber risk: none — both are additive, and `replayAbandonedAt` is an instant, not a storage token. Wire surface: unchanged; `toWireDecision` in channel-web does not carry the new field, and the honesty it buys travels in the receipt sentence instead. | — |

## 2026-08-20 — TASK-218/219/220/221 (the TASK-216/217 follow-up wave)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-20 | TASK-220: fix the conversations seq-race by taking a transaction-scoped `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(conversation_id))` and DELETING the retry loop entirely — not by raising `APPEND_MAX_RETRIES`. | A retry budget is a silent correctness cliff: with k contenders one append can lose k-1 races, so any fixed budget has a concurrency above which events are DROPPED. A deadline-bounded retry is no better — it relocates the cliff and makes it timing-dependent, and a retry loop can starve an append arbitrarily. The lock makes the guarantee unconditional at any concurrency. Precedent already in-repo: `@ax/attachments` uses the identical pattern for its per-user quota gate. | (a) Bump the constant — REJECTED, moves the cliff. (b) Postgres `SEQUENCE` — REJECTED, gaps on rollback break the contiguous-1..N contract the test asserts. (c) Counter side-table — REJECTED, schema change for no gain over the lock. (d) Narrow the test to N=4-6 — REJECTED, knowingly leaves a live defect on the redisplay source of truth. |
| 2026-08-20 | TASK-219: `filterSensitiveMulti` scans fields INDEPENDENTLY rather than joining them. | Not just style — `promotion.ts` joined subject/summary/body with a newline, and `\s` in the password/secret patterns matches a newline, so a field ending in `secret` followed by one starting `:` cross-matched ACROSS the seam. Per-field has no seam and can only REDUCE false positives (every field is still scanned in full), so it can never let through what concatenation caught. | Keep the joined haystack — REJECTED, the seam is a real (if rare) false positive; the helper's doc comment carries the repro so nobody re-joins it. |
| 2026-08-20 | TASK-221: bound the gated-densifier retry with a cache sentinel + cap, rather than emitting a metric and leaving the retry unbounded. | The complaint was "re-pays the LLM every pass forever". A metric only lets you WATCH that happen. The cap actually kills it. The parked entry stores the already-gated fallback plus a count — never the rejected model text — so bounding cost does not create a new place gated content can rest. | Bare metric — REJECTED, observes without fixing. |
| 2026-08-20 | TASK-218: fix only the raw NUL bytes, and add a `scripts/` guard; write `.gitattributes` so the diff is reviewable. | The NUL made whole files invisible to grep (see mistakes.md). Escaping is byte-identical at runtime so no fixture semantics move. `.gitattributes` was NOT cosmetic: git decides binary from EITHER side of a diff pair, so without it a PR whose entire point is "make these readable" would have rendered as `Bin N -> M bytes`. | Blanket-strip the NULs — REJECTED, three of four are load-bearing NUL-injection security fixtures where the NUL is the value under test. |
| 2026-08-20 | Ran the four follow-ups as four parallel worktrees with DISJOINT file ownership, and had NO agent touch `.claude/memory/` — the orchestrator wrote one consolidated entry afterward. | Four agents appending to `decisions.md`/`mistakes.md` produces a four-way merge conflict on the serialized merge; I hit exactly that rebasing TASK-217 against PR #409. Disjoint source files merged with zero conflicts. Trade-off: it deviates from "fold the memory update into the same commit as the work", which is worth it only when several agents run concurrently. | Let each agent write its own memory rows — REJECTED under parallelism (conflict storm); still correct for a solo card. |

## 2026-08-20 — TASK-217 gate the last two LLM-written surfaces that reach `map.md`

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-20 | Gate the **raw** Stage-B class label in `rollup.ts:verifyStageBClasses`, BEFORE `slugify` — not the slug. | Slugification is not redaction, but it IS lossy in a way that makes a slug-level gate mostly theater: measured, `alice@example.com`→`alice-example-com` and `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`→`akiaiosfodnn7example` no longer trip their patterns, while `sk-ant-…` survives. Gating the slug would catch 1 of 6 pattern classes; gating the raw label catches all 6. | Gate the slug (REJECTED — catches almost nothing); gate at `writeRollupDoc` (REJECTED — later, and the label has already been slugified into the doc id by then). |
| 2026-08-20 | A sensitive Stage-B label **drops that class silently**, consistent with every other validation drop in `verifyStageBClasses` (blank label, overlong slug, duplicate slug, sub-K membership all `continue` with no log). Do NOT add a logger param for this one drop reason. | The function is pure `(proposed, residue, config) => DetectedClass[]` with no logger. Logging one drop reason while five stay silent is incoherent observability, and a rollup is a best-effort accelerator — a dropped class degrades to read-time enumeration, it doesn't lose data. If drop-reason observability is wanted it should cover ALL reasons, as its own change. | Add an optional `log` param and warn on the sensitive drop only (REJECTED — incoherent with the sibling drops, widens a pure function's signature for one case). |
| 2026-08-20 | A sensitive **densifier output** in `map.ts` degrades to `fallbackSummary`, logs `memory_strata_map_densify_sensitive` with kinds only, and is **NOT written to the cache**. | Matches the `catch` path in the same function, which returns the fallback WITHOUT caching so the next pass retries — the more security-relevant of the two existing precedents. Caching a sensitive result would freeze it in the sidecar and make the fallback sticky. (Note the empty-output path DOES cache its fallback, so "never cache a fallback" is not an absolute rule here — I am following the catch-path precedent deliberately, not a universal one.) The kinds-only log matches the TASK-216 discipline of never putting matched content in an operator log. | Cache the fallback to avoid re-paying the LLM call each pass (REJECTED — makes a sensitive-triggered degradation permanent and silent). |
| 2026-08-20 | Fix the raw NUL byte in `map.ts` (`h.update(facts.join('\n^@\n'))` → the `\u0000` escape) in THIS PR, as its own commit. | The raw byte makes `file` report the source as `data`, so `grep`/`rg` silently skip the ENTIRE file — it produced a live false negative during this very task (a grep for `filterSensitive` in `map.ts` returned nothing while the import sat at line 43). That directly impairs review of the change I am making to that same file. The escape produces a byte-identical runtime string, so the fact-hash is unchanged and no cached densification is invalidated. Confirmed git still diffs the file as text (the NUL is past git's 8000-byte binary sniff window), so the PR stays reviewable either way. | Leave it (REJECTED — the file stays invisible to code search); change the separator to a non-NUL string (REJECTED — would change every `hashFacts` result, invalidating the whole densify cache and forcing a full re-densify at real LLM cost). |
| 2026-08-20 | Do NOT extract the `filterSensitiveMulti` helper the TASK-216 reviewer suggested; file it as a follow-up instead. | Neither NEW gate in this PR is multi-field — the rollup label and the densifier output are each a single string — so the helper would have zero new consumers and would be a pure refactor of three call sites that merged an hour ago, inflating a security diff. Invariant 4 is about one source of truth for STATE; this is logic duplication, which the reviewer itself classified as "a DRY smell, not a true #4 breach". | Do it here (REJECTED — refactor riding along in a security PR, no new consumer). |
| 2026-08-20 | Four other tracked non-image files carry raw NUL bytes (`memory-strata/src/__tests__/agent-tier-sync.test.ts`, and three under `workspace-git-server`). Card them, don't fix them here. | Out of scope for this card, and several are plausibly deliberate NUL-injection test fixtures that need per-file judgement about whether the raw byte is load-bearing. Only `map.ts` is justified here (it is the file this PR edits). | Fix all five (REJECTED — unrelated packages, needs per-file judgement). |
| 2026-08-20 | No boundary review. | No hook signature or payload changes; both edits are internal to `@ax/memory-strata`. | — |

## 2026-08-20 — TASK-216 sensitive gates scan the LLM-chosen `subject` at both hops

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-20 | On a sensitive `subject`, **reject the whole observation** at BOTH hops (I7 drops it pre-inbox; I11 quarantines the inbox file) — do NOT neutralize `subject` to `'general'` and keep the fact. | Three reasons. (1) It matches the package's own stated posture (`sensitive-gate.ts` header: "False positives drop a useful fact; false negatives leak a credential. We err toward false positives every time."). (2) It matches the closest existing precedent verbatim — `tools/memory-note.ts` (I20) already gates `subject` AND `content` and rejects the whole note if EITHER trips. (3) Neutralizing is actively harmful: `cluster.ts` buckets by `slugify(subject)` and `slugify('general') === 'general'`, so every neutralized observation collapses into ONE `docs/<category>/general.md`, merging unrelated topics and defeating the per-subject clustering that Active Projects, Recent Changes, `memory_search`, and `findNearDupSlug` all depend on. Rejecting changes NOTHING about how surviving observations route. | (a) Neutralize `subject`→`'general'`, keep the fact (the card's own suggestion) — REJECTED for reason (3): silent topic-collapse is a worse failure mode than dropping one over-broad-matched fact, and it would make I7 and I11 asymmetric (I11 cannot neutralize — the subject is already baked into the inbox file's frontmatter and the cluster slug, so its only sane action is the quarantine it already does). (b) Gate only at I11 — REJECTED: I7 is the write-time floor; leaving it open means a credential-shaped subject still lands on disk in `inbox/` and is rendered into Open Threads. |
| 2026-08-20 | I7 merges the `fact` and `subject` rejection kinds into ONE deduplicated `kinds` list (first-seen order) on the existing `RejectedObservation`, rather than adding a `field: 'fact' \| 'subject'` discriminator. | Copies `memory-note.ts`'s existing merge block exactly (one source of truth for the shape of a two-field sensitive rejection). The audit log wants "which patterns fired", not "which field"; naming the field would tell an operator reading the log where in the observation the credential sat, which is marginally more disclosure for no operational gain. No type change ⇒ no consumer churn in `plugin.ts`'s observer audit log. | A `field` discriminator on `RejectedObservation` — REJECTED: type churn + more disclosure, no caller needs it. |
| 2026-08-20 | No boundary review required. | Zero hook signatures or payloads change; `filterSensitive` is already exported from `index.ts`. This is purely an internal widening of two existing in-plugin gates. | — |

## 2026-07-07 — TASK-200 deterministic (Stage A) write-time rollups

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-07-07 | `rollup` is a first-class `DocCategory` requiring FOUR edits (paths `DocCategory`, doc-store `CATEGORIES`, **doc-id `VALID_CATEGORIES`**, types `DocFileType`/`MemoryFileType`) + exclusion from `recent.ts`. All load-bearing. | The doc-id edit is the sneaky one: `parseDocId` gates matchedFacts enrichment (`tools/memory-search.ts`) + the orchestrator map menu + `<load>` guard. Omit it and a retrieved rollup surfaces with NO instance lines on the exact orchestrator path being tuned. Rollups excluded from recent.md (search-time accelerator, not hot-tier). | Add rollup only to the two lists the first draft named — REJECTED (silent no-op on the orchestrator path). |
| 2026-07-07 | Stage-A detection is **per-enumerable-category**: salience denominator = that category's doc count. A class needs df≥K AND df/N ≤ SALIENCE_MAX_FRACTION (0.4). Class slug = pluralize(singularize(token)). Idempotence via a `rollup_hash` frontmatter field over (members, count, instance-line text). | Per-category matches the card's "≤ fraction of the category's docs". The salience gate means a class only materializes when it's a MINORITY pattern (weddings among many episode types) — the year token "2026" or "user" (in ~every doc) is auto-dropped. Storing the hash in frontmatter avoids re-parsing `## Instances` bullets to compare. GOTCHA in tests: with a tiny corpus, adding a member can push a class over 0.4 and DE-qualify it — give enough fillers. | Salience over ALL enumerable docs — REJECTED (card says "the category's docs"). Recompute hash from on-disk body — heavier, fragile bullet re-parse. |
| 2026-07-07 | GC of a de-qualified rollup fires the TASK-199 `memory:doc:deleted { docId }` event INLINE on the CLI/direct path (bus present) AND is RE-FIRED on the k8s tier path after flush (plugin.ts `consolidateRoutedToTier`, symmetric with the existing doc:written re-fire via `reindexTierDocs`). `runRollupPass` returns `deletedDocIds` so the bus-less scratch pass can surface them. | A stale rollup answering `## Count: 3` after its file is gone is wrong-answer-by-construction. The consolidator runs WITHOUT a bus on the tier scratch (events deferred to after flush), so without the re-fire the tier path would leak stale index rows. GC unlinks ONLY `docs/rollup/<slug>.md` with slug ∈ `^[a-z0-9-]+$` (never a raw readdir+unlink). | Fire only on the direct path — REJECTED (tier-path index staleness). Raw readdir+unlink — REJECTED (traversal). |

## 2026-07-01 — TASK-191 promote the retrieval orchestrator (config E) into the Strata runtime

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-07-01 | The runtime seam is the **`memory_search` tool executor** (query-time, tool-driven), NOT a new per-turn augment hook. When an orchestrator client is configured + `retrievalMode:'orchestrator'` (default), memory_search reads `system/map.md` (via the existing inject/tier read path) + the query → runs the orchestrator LLM → executes load/fts ops → returns rows; on miss/timeout/no-client it falls back to plain BM25 (`retrieve`). | The card asks to "decide the seam — tool-driven or per-turn augment". `memory_search` ALREADY carries a real query at turn time (the chat-start inject has none — inject.ts option-b), so it is the natural query-time seam. Zero new hook surface (TASK-190 guidance: read the map via the inject path, no `memory:map:*` hook). The e2e harness already drives `tool:execute:memory_search`, so the acceptance re-run exercises the new path for free. | (a) New per-turn `chat:turn:augment` hook plumbing the user message — REJECTED: bigger kernel change, and inject.ts already documented that as out-of-scope; (b) enhance the chat-start inject — REJECTED: no query at that seam. |
| 2026-07-01 | The orchestrator LLM client is an **injected `OrchestratorClient`** (built by the preset/e2e from host env), defaulting to a **direct-xAI** client; OpenRouter is a fallback only. Implemented with **global `fetch`** (POST api.x.ai / openrouter.ai chat/completions), NOT the `openai`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk` npm SDKs. | Card mandates direct-xAI default (spike: ~400ms p50 vs OpenRouter's ~11s routing artifact) + OpenRouter fallback. A fetch client keeps `openai` OUT of the shipped plugin's RUNTIME deps (it's only a bench devDep today) — no new supply-chain surface in dist. Host-side egress, gated by the host holding `XAI_API_KEY` (same capability class as the Observer's `llm:call:anthropic`), never exposed to the untrusted runner. | (a) Add `openai` as a runtime dep + port the SDK clients verbatim — REJECTED: new supply-chain add to the host for a ~20-line fetch; (b) a new `llm:call:xai` provider plugin/hook — REJECTED: YAGNI, no other consumer, and the card says "client", not "provider". |
| 2026-07-01 | Op grammar is **strictly parsed + whitelisted** to `<load doc=…/>` and `<fts query=…/>` only; a load docId is validated by the SAME traversal guard as memory_read_section (category ∈ closed set, slug `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, no `..`) AND must exist in the agent's own map table before it surfaces a row. | Security-checklist: map summaries + the query (untrusted content, possibly carrying prior-conversation injection) feed the orchestrator LLM. The dominant spike failure was "wrong-session load", not injection, but strict parsing means a crafted injection can at most make the agent load one of ITS OWN docs (owner-routed reads), never traverse out or cross tenants. fts query rides the parameterized BM25 indexer. | Loosely eval the LLM's output / trust arbitrary docIds — REJECTED (prompt-injection surface). |
| 2026-07-01 | `MemoryStrataConfig` gains `retrievalMode?: 'orchestrator' \| 'bm25'` (default `'orchestrator'`) + `orchestrator?: { client; model?; timeoutMs?; topK? }`. No orchestrator vocab leaks into any HOOK payload (there is no new hook); the config field is plugin-internal and the client is opaque. | Card: "config flag to choose orchestrator vs BM25-only default" + "BM25-only as a configurable fallback for latency-sensitive surfaces". `'bm25'` forces pure BM25 even with a client present; `'orchestrator'` + no client degrades to BM25 (acceptance: "degrades to BM25 when the host LLM is absent"). | A boolean `orchestratorEnabled` — REJECTED: a mode enum reads clearer and leaves room for future modes. |

## 2026-07-07 — TASK-205 op-cap reserves fts headroom instead of a blind slice

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-07-07 | `parseOrchestratorPlan` now **reserves `FTS_RESERVE=2` slots for `<fts>` probes** when `<load>` count alone would fill `MAX_OPS` (loadBudget = MAX_OPS − min(2, ftsCount)), instead of collecting all loads then all fts then `slice(0, 8)`. Loads still precede fts in the result. | The blind slice dropped 100% of instance-term `<fts>` probes the moment a counting query emitted ≥8 `<load>` ops, defeating the D3 "for citrus also probe lime/lemon" recall mechanism. Reserving headroom keeps ≥1 probe alive while honoring the MAX_OPS total. | **Interleave load/fts by emission order before slicing** — REJECTED: `runOps` pushes loads first so a `<load>` wins the dedup race against a later `<fts>` hit for the same docId; true emission-order interleave could place an fts before a load and break that documented invariant. Headroom preserves loads-before-fts. |

## 2026-06-29 — TASK-193 undici drift: pin exact 7.28.0 + cap the override at <8.0.0

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-06-29 | Pin `undici` to **exact `7.28.0`** (drop the caret) in `packages/credential-proxy` and `packages/credential-proxy-bridge`, AND cap the root override `undici@>=7.0.0 <7.28.0` replacement from `">=7.28.0"` to `">=7.28.0 <8.0.0"`. | 7.28.0 is the only version that satisfies BOTH constraints: it's the CVE-patched 7.x floor (the override's original intent) AND it's in the 7.x line that's handler-compatible with Node 24's bundled undici 7.18.2 (the global `fetch` the credential-proxy listener + test harness drive with a standalone dispatcher). undici 8.x removed the old handler interface → `invalid onRequestStart method`. Exact pin = the per-package guard (security-critical pkg convention); the override cap = the workspace-wide guard so no `^7.x` consumer can float into 8.x again. An exact `7.28.0` spec doesn't match the override KEY (`<7.28.0`) so it resolves directly regardless of the override. | (a) Update the credential-proxy code to undici 8.x's new handler API — REJECTED: the break is in the TEST harness mixing the global (bundled-7.x) `fetch` with a standalone-8.x dispatcher; you can't change Node's bundled undici, so the only fix is keeping the standalone copy on the same major. (b) Pin only the two packages, leave the override unbounded — REJECTED: leaves the landmine for testcontainers (`^7.24.5`, ~20 pkgs) and any future `^7.x` dep. (c) Cap at `<8.0.0` only, keep carets — REJECTED: the task + security convention require exact pins on this package. |
| 2026-06-29 | Add a behavioural+structural regression guard `undici-handler-compat.test.ts` in credential-proxy rather than relying on the existing 28 tests. | The existing tests DID catch it — but only in the push-to-main full suite (PR CI runs affected-package only), so it stayed red 12 days. A dedicated, minimal guard IN credential-proxy's own suite (asserts standalone-undici major == `process.versions.undici` major, and that a standalone dispatcher drives the global `fetch` without `UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG`) fails loudly in PR CI on the next float, isolating the version contract from the listener machinery. | Rely on existing tests — REJECTED: they only run on main; the gap was CI scope, so a focused canary that's cheap and self-documenting is the durable guard the Bug Fix Policy wants. |

## 2026-06-29 — TASK-192 fair-reranker re-test (local cross-encoder + query expansion + full bodies)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-29 | Add a NEW bench config `f-fair-rerank` (new `ConfigName`) instead of mutating `b-rerank`. | Mutating B would destroy the historical "unfair" zerank-2 baseline and break B's existing config tests; the card explicitly allows "a new config OR extend b-rerank". Research VINDICATES Strata's bets: SmartSearch (arXiv 2603.15599) index-free grep+reranker = 88.4% LME-S (~1pp off embeddings); "Does Memory Need Graphs?" (arXiv 2601.01280) finds foundational settings, not graph/embeddings, drive accuracy. | (B) adopt OSS wholesale — rejected (embeddings dep + unverified numbers). (C) hybrid swap of retrieval internals — folded into the orchestrator+map decision below. |

Our OWN LongMemEval-S spikes already settled this: config B (BM25 + zerank-2 reranker) LOST to BM25-only (−2.4pp, ~6× slower); vectors lost badly (config C, −9pp); config E (orchestrator + BM25 fallback) + LLM-rewritten map BEAT BM25-only by +7.6pp accuracy / +14.2pp recall@5 (n=500), clearing the ≥5-pt bar, and improved abstention (correct-refusal 70%→81.5%). Map-summary QUALITY is the load-bearing lever. Orchestrator latency ≈400ms via direct xAI (the ~7s in the report was an OpenRouter routing artifact), ≈5× BM25. | The deep-research "add a cross-encoder reranker" idea is pre-empted by local evidence against a reranker — caveat: zerank-2 (hosted, on truncated bodies, BM25-only candidate pool) ≠ SmartSearch's local mxbai cross-encoder + query expansion, so re-testable but not a slam-dunk. | Add a reranker — deprioritized (lost locally; logged in TASK-191 body so it isn't re-litigated). |

## 2026-06-08 — TASK-164 Plan 2 (cwd=HOME=/workspace + re-root .ax/**+.claude/** → /agent)

filestore-user-files design §8-9, Phase 2. When `AX_USERFILES_ROOT` is set (durable
NFS user-files mount wired by the sandbox provider), the claude-sdk runner reshapes the
agent's frame; unset = today's behavior (cwd=HOME=/agent), no broadening.

Decisions:
- **Effective HOME/cwd = `userFilesRoot` when set, else `workspaceRoot`.** Compute one
  `sdkHome`/`sdkCwd` value up front and feed it to BOTH the SDK `HOME:` env and `cwd:`.
  Everything else (git ops, transcript symlink scaffolding `scaffoldSdkProjectsSymlink`,
  prompt-engine `.ax` reads, uploads materialization, commit/bundle diff) STAYS on
  `env.workspaceRoot` (=/agent, the governed git tier). Only the *agent's working frame*
  moves; the *governed frame* does not. This is the whole point of Plan 2 (design §8).
- **home-bin PATH derives from the effective HOME, not workspaceRoot.** `buildHomeBinEnv(sdkHome, …)`
  → `~/bin` = `/workspace/bin` (durable NFS), so installed binaries persist live, NOT via
  git bundle. `~/bin` is no longer git-bundled (it's on the separate /workspace mount,
  outside the /agent git root). Container `.bashrc` already uses `$HOME/bin` literally —
  no Dockerfile change needed (it follows HOME wherever it points).
- **Re-rooter broadened to ALL `.ax/**` + `.claude/**` (+ root-exact `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md`),
  gated on userFilesRoot set.** Imports `POLICY_PREFIXES` + `POLICY_EXACT_PATHS` from
  `@ax/core` (the kernel — allowed by eslint; runner gains a NEW `@ax/core` dep) so the
  re-root scope and the validator policy scope share ONE source of truth (invariant 4). If
  they drifted, agent self-edits could land on ungoverned NFS — the §14 governance linchpin.
  The existing `.ax/uploads/` re-root is now a subset of `.ax/**`.
- **Re-root TARGET is `workspaceRoot` (=/agent), unchanged.** A matched governed path
  (bare `.ax/x`, cwd-prefixed `/workspace/.ax/x`, home-prefixed `/home/u/.ax/x`, already
  `/agent/.ax/x`) maps to `<workspaceRoot>/<rel>`. Idempotent on already-correct paths;
  refuses `..` traversal segments (kept from the uploads re-rooter); only rewrites the
  structured path keys (file_path/path/notebook_path), never free-text fields.
- **When userFilesRoot UNSET: re-rooter unchanged (uploads-only).** The broadened match is
  conditional so today's deployments are byte-identical. Avoids re-rooting `.claude/` paths
  the agent legitimately writes when cwd=HOME=/agent (there's no NFS to drift onto).
- **workspaceNote prose made cwd-aware.** With cwd=/workspace the old "`/agent` is your
  current working directory" line is factually wrong and would misdirect `.ax/uploads`
  resolution. Note now states the working dir (effective cwd) separately from the governed
  root (/agent) that attachments resolve under. In-scope: the cwd move broke the note.
- **Regression coverage:** transcript resolution is cwd-independent (symlink + slug-agnostic
  readdir-walk), prompt-engine `.ax` reads stay on /agent, skill discovery is
  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR-based (HOME/cwd-independent) — assert these don't move.
- **(security-checklist) Re-rooter must NOT over-capture nested governed dirs.** The
  validator's `filterToPolicy` governs only GIT-ROOT-RELATIVE top-level `.ax/`+`.claude/`.
  A naive "match `.claude/` anywhere as a segment" over-captures a user's cloned-repo
  `/workspace/myrepo/.claude/` and yanks it to /agent — corrupting the user's repo AND
  diverging from the validator. FIX: the broadened re-rooter (`findGovernedSegment`) matches
  a governed segment ONLY at the TOP LEVEL of a recognized root: offset 0 (bare relative),
  or immediately after a `recognizedRoots` entry (cwd=sdkHome + ephemeral, passed from
  main.ts; workspaceRoot auto-added), or after `~/` / a single-segment `/home/<user>/` home
  dir (the dotfile illusion — but NOT a deeper `/home/<user>/projects/.ax`). The legacy
  `.ax/uploads/` re-rooter keeps mid-path matching (its namespace is specific enough to be
  safe). Unit-tested both ways. The `..`-traversal refusal is kept from the uploads re-rooter.
- **(security-checklist note for PR):** Sandbox — re-rooter is a NARROWING control (governed
  paths → /agent before host adjudication), never widens; `..` refused, top-level-only match,
  additionalDirectories grants only the 4 documented tiers. Injection — untrusted tool-input
  paths only re-rooted on structured path keys, never shell/SQL/URL/prompt; free-text fields
  untouched; host tool.pre-call still adjudicates. Supply chain — one new dep `@ax/core`
  (workspace:* in-repo kernel, already the universal allowed import; no scripts/transitive).

## 2026-06-07 — TASK-170 harden runner-pod teardown (killPod retry + orphan sweep)

A warm runner pod that exits clean (Succeeded) can be ORPHANED forever if the host's
single `deleteNamespacedPod` hits a transient apiserver 5xx (observed GKE Standard:
`HTTP 500 rpc error: code = Unavailable ... throttled ... (memory-protection)`), because
(1) `killPod` did a SINGLE delete with no retry, (2) both call sites in open-session.ts
wrap it in `.catch(() => undefined)` (swallow the rethrow), and (3) runner pods are bare
Pods with NO ownerReference, so no controller/GC ever reclaims them.

Decisions:
- **killPod gains a bounded retry** on TRANSIENT errors only. Transient = 5xx
  (statusCode/code/response.statusCode in 500–599) OR a message matching
  `/unavailable|throttl|overloaded|timeout|ServiceUnavailable/i` (the observed shape is a
  500 carrying `code = Unavailable`). 404/NotFound stays the happy path (no retry —
  `isPodGoneError`). 4xx (≠404) is PERMANENT (bad-request/forbidden) → do NOT retry,
  rethrow immediately. Default 3 attempts, backoff 250→500→1000ms, with a testable
  `sleep` seam (mirrors lifecycle.ts `waitForPodReady`). Total ≪ the 300s service timeout.
  Rationale: the throttle is brief; a couple of retries clears it. Alternatives rejected:
  unbounded retry (could hang teardown); retry-everything (would hammer the apiserver on a
  genuine 403/permanent error).
- **Periodic orphan-sweep** added to the plugin (init starts it, shutdown clears it) —
  the established attachments-janitor pattern (setInterval + clearInterval + await
  in-flight + `makeAgentContext` init logger + `unref()` so it never pins the process).
  Lists runner-namespace pods scoped by `labelSelector: app.kubernetes.io/component=ax-next-runner`
  (NEVER touches host/other pods), filters to terminal phase (Succeeded|Failed) whose
  `metadata.creationTimestamp` is older than N minutes, and deletes them. Defaults:
  sweep every 5 min, reap terminal pods older than 10 min (safely past the 5s grace +
  ~2s retry window of a normal teardown). This is the self-heal: a delete that still
  ultimately fails gets reclaimed on the next sweep. RBAC ALREADY grants
  `pods: create/delete/get/list/watch` (deploy/charts/ax-next/templates/host/role.yaml) —
  NO new capability grant needed.
- **ownerReference / Job-with-ttlSecondsAfterFinished DEFERRED** as a follow-up (bigger
  change). Tradeoff: an ownerReference to the host pod would let k8s GC reap a runner when
  the host dies, and a Job with ttlSecondsAfterFinished would auto-reap finished pods — but
  both are larger reworks of pod-spec + the create path, and the retry+sweep already gives
  belt-and-suspenders self-healing for the observed failure. Filed as a follow-up card.
- **No hook-surface change.** The retry is internal to killPod; the sweep is internal to the
  plugin. `K8sCoreApi.listNamespacedPod` gains optional `labelSelector` in `PodListRequest`
  (the real ObjectParamAPI CoreV1Api already accepts it; verified against the pinned
  @kubernetes/client-node@1.4.0 `ObjectParamAPI.d.ts`). No boundary review needed (internal
  impl only).

Optional + back-compat: older clients ignore it. | (a) overload `reason` with the full message — rejected: dropped client-side + violates the "stable code, no pod name" contract. Size-bound + extract-don't-echo prevents a malicious image from injecting a wall of text / ANSI / fake instructions into the author's error card. ## 2026-06-03 — TASK-145 Harden flush-workspace-host.e2e teardown vs ENOTEMPTY rmdir mirror.git/info race

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-03 | Root cause of the `flush-workspace-host.e2e.test.ts` `afterEach` flake `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '.../mirror.git/info'` (signature `ci:flush-workspace-host.e2e:ENOTEMPTY-rmdir-mirror-info`) is a **teardown rmdir-vs-detached-git-write race**, distinct from the TASK-137 assertion flake and the TASK-5 timeout flake. Each test stands up a REAL bare git mirror under the per-test scratch dir; git's `gc.autoDetach` defaults TRUE (git 2.52.0), so a push/fetch/receive-pack can spawn a `git gc --auto` that **detaches into a background process** and keeps writing into `mirror.git/info` (`update-server-info` writes `info/refs`; gc packs refs) AFTER the foreground git the test awaited exited. `afterEach`'s recursive `fs.rm` then `rmdir`s `mirror.git/info` while it's momentarily non-empty → ENOTEMPTY. Fix: a test-scoped `rmScratch(dir)` helper (`src/__tests__/rm-scratch.ts`) doing `fs.rm(dir,{recursive,force,maxRetries:10,retryDelay:25})`; the `afterEach` calls it. | `fs.rm({force:true})` does NOT retry ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY — `force` only suppresses "path does not exist"; ONLY `maxRetries`+`retryDelay` enable Node's backoff-retry that rides out the transient race. HARNESS-ONLY: production never `fs.rm`s a live mirror (host mirror = long-lived storage; runner `commit-notify-resync.ts` is all awaited, no fire-and-forget) — so the fix is test-teardown-only, no runner behaviour change. PROVEN by a standalone repro: a writer churning files into an `info/` dir while `fs.rm` removes the tree threw ENOTEMPTY 32/60 with `{recursive,force}` and 0/60 with `maxRetries`. TDD red-check: neuter rmScratch (strip maxRetries) → the regression test throws the EXACT `ENOTEMPTY … rmdir '.../mirror.git/info'`; restore → green. ## 2026-06-01 — TASK-137 De-flake flush-workspace-host.e2e BUG-W2 resync assertion (residual from TASK-123)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-01 | Root cause of the `flush-workspace-host.e2e.test.ts > "host-side delete … resyncs cleanly"` **assertion** flake (not a timeout — file ~607ms): the test's `makeHostClient` mock runs **real, fallible `git` subprocesses inside its IPC handlers** (`workspace.commit-notify`→`mirrorMain` rev-parse + `fetchBundleAdvance` fetch; `workspace.export-baseline-bundle`→`bundle create`). Under CI's severe multi-package + Docker-testcontainer starvation a SINGLE transient git subprocess hiccup (spawn EAGAIN / a starved non-zero exit) anywhere in the flush→retire→commit→resync sequence is correctly mapped by production `commitNotifyWithResync` to a DEGRADED outcome (`'kept'` on a thrown commit-notify call; `'rolled-back'` when a transient `rev-parse` returns null → mock omits `actualParent`). The test then asserts `res.outcome==='accepted'` → `expected 'kept' to be 'accepted'`. PROVEN by fault injection: throwing on the resync-retry commit-notify deterministically yields `resyncOutcome=kept`. The git LOGIC is deterministic (200× clean standalone sequence; clean even with a dirty-tree `--autostash`); only the subprocess *scheduling under starvation* is not. | This matches the card exactly (assertion flake, not timeout; the host-delete→flush→runner-commit resync path). It is NOT a git-ordering race (the parent-mismatch is structural: runner parent=foo-tip vs mirror head=retire) and NOT a fire-and-forget/wall-clock race like memory-strata's Observer — so there is no un-awaited promise to await. The "ordering luck" the card names is the implicit bet that all ~6 fallible git subprocesses in the mock succeed on the FIRST try under load. | (a) bump per-test `testTimeout` — useless, it's not a timeout (rejected); (b) `.skip` — loses real BUG-W2/resync coverage (rejected); (c) loosen the assertion to accept `kept`/`rolled-back` — masks a genuine "resync didn't land" regression (rejected). |
| 2026-06-01 | Fix: add a bounded **transient-failure retry seam** to the test's `git()` helper (and the mock's git calls route through it) so a starvation-induced spawn-EAGAIN / transient non-zero git exit is retried-to-completion ("settle") rather than treated as authoritative and mistranslated into a degraded outcome. Regression test: a fault-injecting mock variant that fails a git op on its first attempt and asserts the retry seam still drives the resync to `accepted`. | This is the "await the resync settle via a test seam, not ordering luck" the card asks for, adapted to the actual mechanism (fallible subprocess, not un-awaited async). It keeps the test exercising the REAL resync path while removing the starvation dependence. Production code is UNCHANGED (the degradation behavior is correct; the bug is the TEST betting every git fork succeeds first try). | bump global timeouts (wrong class); add retry to PRODUCTION `runGit` (out of scope + would change real degradation semantics — rejected). |

## 2026-06-01 — TASK-124 Per-slot credential refs (settings-unified epic, keystone)

- **The collapse-vs-expand rule keys on `connector.capabilities.credentials.length` (the connector's slot COUNT), NOT on whether two slots resolve to the same service tag.** Spec is explicit: exactly 1 slot → `account:<service>` (byte-identical to today, no migration); ≥2 slots → `account:<service>:<slot>` per slot. Rationale: the design wants a connector that declares e.g. CLIENT_ID + CLIENT_SECRET to get two distinct vault rows even though both fall back to the same service tag (the connectorId) — that's the collision being fixed. Keying on count is the design's stated rule and is the simplest deterministic predicate every mirror can reproduce from the connector it already holds.
- **`Destination.account` gains optional `slot`; `refForDestination` reconstructs from it.** `{kind:'account', service, slot}` → `account:<service>:<slot>` when `slot` present, else `account:<service>`. The PRESENCE of `slot` on the destination (set by the caller per the count rule) drives collapse-vs-expand at the ref layer — `refForDestination` stays a pure deterministic function of its input, no count logic inside it. `assertNoColon` runs on `slot` too (slot names are SCREAMING_SNAKE `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` per @ax/connectors SLOT_RE — no colon, safe to append). All 3 mirrors + refs-fixtures.ts add a multi-slot fixture (`{service:'github', slot:'GITHUB_TOKEN'}` → `account:github:GITHUB_TOKEN`) AND keep the single-slot fixture (`{service:'linear'}` → `account:linear`) — the byte-identical back-compat assertion.
- **`accountRef` becomes `accountRef(service, slot?)` — the single ref-builder used by `deriveCredentialPlan` (both mirrors) and re-derived in the orchestrator fold.** `deriveCredentialPlan` computes `isMulti = connector.capabilities.credentials.length >= 2` once, then maps each slot to `ref: accountRef(serviceTagForSlot(slot, id), isMulti ? slot.slot : undefined)`. `serviceTagForSlot` unchanged. The orchestrator's `foldConnectorCaps` / `connector-card.ts` re-derive the SAME `isMulti`-gated ref locally (I2 — no @ax/connectors import), pinned by connector-union.test.ts / connector-card.test.ts.
- **`CredentialPlanEntry` gains the destination-shaping bits so the connect-flow UI does NOT string-parse the ref.** ConnectorConnectDialog today does `entry.ref.slice('account:'.length)` to rebuild `{kind:'account', service}` — that breaks for `account:<service>:<slot>` (would yield service=`<service>:<slot>`, failing the account regex). Instead the plan entry carries the structured `account` + optional `slotTag` (or the destination directly) so the UI builds `{kind:'account', service, slot?}` without parsing. This keeps WRITE (card/dialog → setDestinationCredential → refForDestination) and READ (orchestrator fold → resolve vault) addressing the SAME row. Both deriveCredentialPlan copies (connectors + channel-web) carry the field.
- **PermissionCard's two write paths (skill `approveSkill`, connector `approveConnector`) must also emit the per-slot destination.** They currently build `{kind:'account', service: s.account ?? request.connectorId}`. The card's `slots[]` (from connector-card.ts / request-capability.ts) must gain the per-slot `account`+`slotTag` (or a `multiSlot` flag) so the card writes to the same per-slot ref the orchestrator fold reads. `haveExisting` in connector-card.ts / request-capability.ts likewise checks the per-slot ref.
- **Verify-before-merge (acceptance bullet 5): no existing multi-slot connector relies on the colliding `account:<connectorId>` ref.** Checked the codebase — there are NO seeded/default multi-slot connectors; the only connectors are test fixtures + admin-authored at runtime. Single-slot back-compat means zero migration for the common case; the per-slot change only activates for ≥2-slot connectors, of which none exist with stored keys. Documented in PR.
- **No new service-hook signature.** `credentials:{set,get,list,delete}` unchanged — the ref STRING is shaped differently, that's all. Only `Destination` (+ its 3 mirrors + DestinationSchema) gains optional `slot`. Boundary-review: not a new hook surface.
- **`CredentialSlotForm` static `id="cred-payload"` was a latent multi-instance id COLLISION** — harmless until a multi-slot connector renders one form per slot (ConnectorConnectDialog). Fixed with `useId()` per instance (label `htmlFor` association); the label text stays "API key" (NOT the slot name) so the existing `getByLabelText(/api key/i)` tests + the parent dialog's `<p>{slot}</p>` heading both hold. The in-chat PermissionCard renders its OWN per-slot Input (`id=perm-cred-<slot>`, labelled by slot name) — unaffected.
- **`UserSkillsPanelBody.tsx` authored-skill early-approve slot-write loop is effectively DEAD** — `@ax/skills` `pendingCapabilitiesFor` always returns `{}` post-TASK-100 (a skill carries no caps; reach is its connectors, gated by the connector card). So `AuthoredSkillListing.pendingCapabilities` is never populated; its `{kind:'account', service: s.account}` write is the collapsed single-slot form and never sees a multi-slot connector. Left unchanged (changing it = gold-plating dead code); NOT a correctness gap.
- **Verify-before-merge (acceptance bullet 5) CONFIRMED empirically:** no seeded connectors, no migration-inserted connectors (migrations only ADD COLUMNs); all connectors created at runtime by admins/authoring. No multi-slot connector with stored keys exists → the colliding `account:<connectorId>` ref has no live dependents → zero migration needed.

## 2026-06-01 — TASK-109 User-facing connector connect flow (keyMode JIT vs shared-key consent)

- **The connect flow derives the credential plan + consent gate CLIENT-SIDE from the full `Connector` (`getConnector(id)`), NOT a `connectors:resolve` BFF call.** There is no HTTP route for `connectors:resolve` — only the 5 `/admin/connectors[/:id]` CRUD routes; `getConnector` already returns `capabilities`. So TASK-96's derivation (`deriveCredentialPlan`/`requiresSharedKeyConsent`/`sharedKeyConsentMessage`/`accountRef`/`serviceTagForSlot`) is **re-declared locally in `lib/connectors.ts`** — mirroring the existing local `refForDestination` re-declaration in `lib/credentials.ts`. Rationale: `@ax/connectors` is NOT on eslint's runtime-import allowlist (only `@ax/credentials` is among the credential-ish plugins), and channel-web doesn't even devDepend on it; a runtime import is an I2 violation. A unit test pins the local behavior + the EXACT `SHARED_KEY_CONSENT_COPY` string (the consent text is a security contract). Alternatives rejected: (a) add a `connectors:resolve` HTTP route + lib wrapper → new wire surface for data `getConnector` already carries; half-extra. (b) add `@ax/connectors` to the import allowlist for a drift-guard runtime import → widens the cross-plugin runtime surface for a test convenience; the `refForDestination` precedent is local-re-decl + pin-by-test, not allowlist-widening.
- **keyMode → write route is the EXISTING destination-credential split, no new wire:** `personal`→`scope:'user'` via `setDestinationCredential`→`/settings/destinations/account/credential` (server forces ownerId=actor, any authed user); `workspace`→`scope:'global'` via `/admin/destinations/account/credential` (`requireAdmin`). The consent gate is the design's "act as you" moment surfaced BEFORE the workspace key-entry form is reachable; `requiresSharedKeyConsent` = `keyMode==='workspace' || visibility==='shared'`. A non-admin opening a workspace connector can't store the global key (admin route is admin-gated) → surface "an admin provides this shared key", not a raw 403. Destination = `{kind:'account', service: slot.account ?? connectorId}` → ref `account:<service>` — the SAME row TASK-96/97/112 read/write (divergent-ref trap avoided).
- **Connected/not = REAL credential presence, mirroring `CredentialSlotRow`.** Fetch `myCredentials.list()` (user-plan slots) / `adminCredentials.list()` (global-plan slots) once, match `c.ref===ref && c.scope===planScope`; connected iff every plan slot has a stored credential. **Empty plan** (no credential slots — an MCP-no-key connector) ⇒ connected (nothing to prompt). The user list only returns the actor's own creds, so ref+scope match suffices (the JIT account flow already writes with `ownerId:null`).

## 2026-06-01 — TASK-116 KeysTab/CredentialsTab humane errors, no raw-ref leak, friendlier service field

- **Friendlier "Service" field = relabel + silent slugify, NOT a picker.** The card asks for "a friendlier label/picker that does not expose slug grammar." There is NO service catalog anywhere in the codebase — `account:<service>` is a free-form slug any skill slot binds to via `account: <service>`; the only sources of service NAMES are the connectors list + the account-usage map (services already referenced). A true picker would need a new catalog wire surface (YAGNI / out of scope). Save enabled iff `toServiceSlug(input).length>0 && value.length>0`. Inferable from code+conventions (not a human product call): the contract row is unchanged, grammar is enforced silently rather than surfaced.
- **Humane error = sibling pattern + fixed next-step.** Replace the 5 `setError(String(e))` with a module-level `humanError(e) = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` (exact ConnectorsTab/ConnectorConnectDialog idiom). The destructive Alert leads with the card-mandated next-step sentence ("We couldn't save your key. Check it's correct and try again — your admin can help if it keeps failing.") and shows the technical message as a secondary muted detail.

Rows stay read-only.
- **No hook/IPC/boundary/dep change — pure channel-web UI; security-checklist not triggered** (untrusted ref text still renders through auto-escaped React text nodes, same as before).
- **Review (Phase 5, ran `/code-review --effort high` — the `ax-code-reviewer` Task subagent isn't available in this env, logged substitution) caught a prototype-key footgun:** `OTHER_KIND_LABEL[kind] ?? 'Other credential'` returns the INHERITED function for `kind==='toString'`/`'constructor'` (and an object for `'__proto__'`), which would crash the row render. Fixed with `Object.hasOwn(OTHER_KIND_LABEL, kind)` + regression test. General rule for a plain-object lookup keyed by ANY external string (even server-issued metadata): guard with `Object.hasOwn` / `Object.create(null)` / a `Map` — a bare `obj[k] ?? fallback` leaks the prototype chain.

NOT a backing-mechanism leak (`defaultAttached` is a storage-agnostic curation boolean already on the full `Connector` + every other hook shape; leak-guard `LEAKY_FIRST_CLASS_FIELDS` excludes it). ## 2026-06-01 — TASK-114 Connectors walk polish: re-propose dedup + Vite /settings dev-proxy

- **Re-propose dedup belongs in `connectors:install-authored`, NOT the orchestrator card path or the `connector_propose` tool.** Bug (TASK-101 walk): a warm-turn re-propose of an ALREADY-ACTIVE connector reset the authored draft to `pending`, and `fireUpfrontConnectorCards` (orchestrator) re-fired the upfront approval card every turn (it keys off a pending draft; `applyAuthoredConnectorGrant` clears `upfrontConnectorCardsByConv` on approval so every warm turn re-evaluates). Root cause = `installAuthoredConnector` always (re)wrote a pending draft with no check against the registry TASK-113 promoted into. Fix at the single chokepoint: pass the plugin's OWN live `localStore` (the registry, `ConnectorStore`) into the handler alongside the authored-draft store (both same-plugin → no cross-plugin import, no new `calls` edge), and BEFORE upserting, `registry.getByIdNotDeleted(ownerUserId, connectorId)` — if non-null it's a NO-OP (write nothing, return `{connectorId, status:'active'}`). No pending draft re-created ⟹ orchestrator card path sees nothing to card. ONE fix covers BOTH acceptance sub-points. The tool path needed no parallel guard (it calls the hook).
- **Equivalence rule = pure id match, owner-scoped (simplest-correct, per the card's scoping note).** An active (not-deleted) registry connector owned by the SAME user with the SAME connector id. NOT a capability-fill comparison (that would be a product decision the card said to avoid). `getByIdNotDeleted` already filters `owner_user_id` + `deleted_at IS NULL`, so: (a) a different user's connector never triggers dedup (pinned by a cross-owner test), and (b) a SOFT-DELETED (un-approved/removed) connector returns null → falls through to the normal pending+card path → re-approval required (correct security posture — tombstone never silently resurrects reach).
- **Wire change = widen `InstallAuthoredOutput.status` `'pending'` → `'pending'|'active'`** (+ its zod `InstallAuthoredOutputSchema` union + the `@ax/tool-connector-propose` `ConnectorProposeOutput.status` mirror, which already passes `out.status` through). Only hook-surface change; `status` is a lifecycle verdict, storage/transport-agnostic, no leak; no boundary-review concern. SECURITY: the short-circuit only fires when an ALREADY-APPROVED (human-gated, TASK-113-promoted) connector exists — it grants ZERO new reach (writes nothing) and cannot escalate/bypass approval; if no registry match, the pending+card path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Vite dev-proxy `/settings` gap (item 2):** `packages/channel-web/vite.config.ts` proxy forwarded only `/auth`,`/admin`,`/api` to `AX_BACKEND_URL`; the connector connect/credential write POSTs to `/settings/*`, so a local Vite walk 404'd. Added `'/settings': { target: backendUrl, changeOrigin: false, ws: false }`. Config-only, no test: the MOCK middleware (offline mode) has no `/settings` connector handlers and the walk uses PROXY mode (real backend); real deploys are same-origin so unaffected. (Distinct config from TASK-106 but same dev-parity theme.)
- **Alternatives rejected:** (a) dedup in the orchestrator `fireUpfrontConnectorCards` card path → symptom-patch, leaves the spurious pending draft (fails acceptance sub-point 1's "no pending draft re-created"). (b) dedup in the `connector_propose` tool → the tool has no registry access without an `@ax/connectors` runtime import (I2 violation). (c) capability-fill equivalence → product decision, out of scope.

## 2026-05-31 — TASK-104 Fix postgres-testcontainer teardown 57P01 flake at root

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-31 | Fix the uncaught `57P01` ("terminating connection due to administrator command") teardown flake with ONE shared helper `stopPostgresContainer(container)` in `@ax/test-harness`, and migrate all 105 postgres-testcontainer suites (106 call sites) to call it in `afterAll` in place of `await container.stop()`. The helper installs a temporary `uncaughtException`+`unhandledRejection` guard that swallows ONLY the benign 57P01 shape (by `code==='57P01'` OR the message substring), awaits `container.stop()` + one macrotask tick (the socket error surfaces async AFTER stop() resolves), then removes its listeners. No-ops on `undefined`. | Root-caused + reproduced: when `container.stop()` SIGTERMs postgres, the server kills every connection still bound to an OPEN `pg.Pool`. A test-created `pg.Pool` has NO `'error'` listener, so Node re-emits the connection error as an **uncaughtException** — and vitest counts an uncaught exception during teardown as a suite failure even when every assertion passed (exact card symptom "This error originated ... while it was running"; control run = `Tests 1 passed / Errors 1 error → EXIT 1`, helper run = EXIT 0). The card's two options are "drain pools before stop" (already mostly done in per-package `afterEach`, but a tick-late socket error still races) and "swallow the benign 57P01" — the helper does the swallow as a deterministic BACKSTOP so the residual race can't red the suite, applied through one helper to avoid per-package drift (the card's stated preference). Typed against a minimal `{ stop(): Promise<unknown> }` so `@ax/test-harness` does NOT take a runtime dep on `@testcontainers/postgresql`. Every postgres package already devDepends on `@ax/test-harness`, so no package.json changes. | (a) Per-package `afterEach` pool-draining only — rejected: it's necessary but not sufficient; the error surfaces a tick AFTER `destroy()`/`close()` resolves and races `container.stop()`, and TASK-94 already saw it red CI despite drained pools. (b) A global vitest `setupFiles` process guard installed for the WHOLE run — rejected: it would mask a real 57P01 raised DURING a test (not just teardown); scoping the guard to the `stop()` window keeps real errors loud. (c) `fileParallelism:false` / serialize the suites — rejected: masks the race, slows CI, doesn't root-cause. (d) Add `pool.on('error')` to every test pool — rejected: ~100-file churn vs one helper, and still leaves the unawaited-rejection variant. |

## 2026-05-31 — TASK-89 Make server early-bind authoritative (retry bind + 503 POST) to close cold-respawn 404 at the source

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-31 | **Replace the single best-effort early-bind in `channel-web/src/server/routes-chat.ts` `postMessage` with a bounded-retry loop, then 503 the POST if the bind never lands.** New helper `bindActiveReqIdAuthoritative(bus, ctx, {conversationId, sessionId, reqId, logger})` → boolean. Loop: capped-exponential backoff (start 25ms, ×2, cap ~150ms) gated on a `Date.now()+BIND_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS` deadline (BIND_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS=400). On success → return true (→ 202). On bind throw → keep the existing `chat_bind_session_failed` warn telemetry, sleep the clamped backoff, retry. Budget spent → return false → POST `res.status(503).json({error:'bind-unavailable'})`. | Card contract is "retry the bind, then 503 the POST if it can't be established." 400ms is small (sub-perceptible to a user; the SSE GET race is microseconds) yet absorbs a read-after-write replica lag race or a brief DB blip — the realistic transient causes of a first-try bind failure when the row was JUST created/fetched in the same request. The happy path binds first try (one call, zero added latency) → 202 exactly as today. 503 (not 202) on persistent failure means the client never gets a reqId whose `GET /api/chat/stream/:reqId` can never 200 — it surfaces the existing CONNECTION_LOST banner + manual retry (TASK-88's client path), which re-POSTs the whole turn. This fix REDUCES how often TASK-88's ~30s client SSE-open budget is even exercised (the 404 window no longer opens on the happy path), without contradicting it. | (a) keep single best-effort + rely only on TASK-88's client retry (rejected: that's the mitigation, not the source fix this card asks for; leaves the 404 window open); (b) await the orchestrator's post-open-session bind instead (rejected: that's seconds later for a cold pod — the exact latency this closes; and routes-chat fires agent:invoke fire-and-forget, it can't await the orchestrator); (c) huge retry budget / unbounded (rejected: a genuinely-missing conversation would hang the POST; 400ms bounds it and 503 lets the client retry cleanly). |
| 2026-05-31 | **If `bus.hasService('conversations:bind-session')` is false, return 503 immediately (do not 202).** Keep the `hasService` guard (matches the orchestrator's identical convention — bind-session is NOT a manifest-declared call; both routes-chat and orchestrator.ts gate it via `hasService`). | A bind service that isn't registered means the bind can NEVER be established → a 202 would hand back a reqId whose stream can never open, which is exactly the failure this card kills. In prod the k8s preset ALWAYS co-deploys @ax/conversations (verified: only preset booting channel-web, and it boots conversations), so this branch is effectively unreachable in prod; it's the correct contract-honoring fallback for a degenerate preset. Not declaring it in the manifest preserves the established peer convention and keeps blast radius off every harness's verifyCalls walk. | (a) promote bind-session to a hard manifest `call` (rejected: churns every channel-web test harness's verifyCalls + diverges from the orchestrator's hasService convention for the SAME hook — one source of truth for the convention); (b) keep silent fall-through to 202 when absent (rejected: that's the bug — 202 for an un-openable reqId). |
| 2026-05-31 | **Phase-5 review substitution: the `ax-code-reviewer` subagent + the Agent/Task dispatch tool were UNAVAILABLE in this orchestrated env (same gap as TASK-87/34/35), so I ran the `code-review` skill — whose finder/verifier angles ALSO need the Agent tool — and performed its 9 angles myself directly over the in-context whole-branch `main...HEAD` diff.** No actionable findings: the retry loop is bounded (no infinite spin — `remaining<=0` returns false before sleeping; wait clamped to remaining budget; happy path = 1 call, returns true immediately); telemetry + `existingActiveSessionId ?? placeholder` behavior preserved; the only behavior change (absent service / persistent failure → 503 instead of silent 202) is the card's intent. REUSE angle: no shared backoff/retry util exists (`@ax/core/util` has only safe-path + with-timeout; transport.ts's client loop is a different runtime/semantics — I2 makes a cross-boundary util premature), so inlining matches precedent. Test-race check: `chatRunMockPlugin`'s `agent:invoke` mock does NOT call `conversations:bind-session`, so the happy-path `bindCalls===1` assertion is deterministic (not racy on the fire-and-forget orchestrator bind). The PR's hosted reviewers (CodeRabbit/CodeQL/semgrep/gitleaks) are the second pair of eyes in CI. | Block on the missing subagent (rejected: env capability gap, not a code issue; small additive pure-control-flow diff, 7 tests, hosted-reviewer-covered). | — |
| 2026-05-31 | **Scope strictly server-side (channel-web) — do NOT touch transport.ts.** The card's "client retries the whole turn" is already satisfied: transport.ts `sendMessages` throws on any non-OK POST → runtime onError → CONNECTION_LOST-class banner + manual retry (a deliberate re-POST). A POST 503 flows through that existing path unchanged. | Card explicitly says "Scope (server-side — channel-web)". TASK-88 owns the client. Auto-re-POSTing a 503 client-side would risk duplicating a turn (FAULTA-5 forbids automated re-POST) — the manual-retry affordance is the safe re-POST path. | (a) auto-retry the POST in transport (rejected: out of scope + FAULTA-5 duplicate-turn hazard); (b) special-case 503 vs other POST failures client-side (rejected: out of scope; the existing banner already handles it). |

## 2026-05-30 — TASK-79 skill_propose manifest contract align + close capability-loss gate bypass (SECURITY)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-30 | **Fix the capability-loss bypass AT THE PARSER (`parseSkillManifest`), not at the gate: hard-reject (`invalid-manifest`) any of `allowedHosts`/`credentials`/`mcpServers`/`packages` declared at the TOP LEVEL of a manifest (outside `capabilities:`).** | The card framed it as "the gate must classify pending", but the gate (`classifyProposal`) was already correct — it classifies on its input. The bug was upstream: the parser read caps ONLY from `doc['capabilities']`, so top-level cap keys were SILENTLY DROPPED → the proposal parsed to zero caps → gate saw origin=authored + zero-cap → `active`. The single-source-of-truth fix is to make the parser (the one contract authority, shared by global/user/authored/promote flows) reject the misplaced keys, so a dropped/stripped-cap manifest is a loud structural reject regardless of which flow or which doc drift produced it. Defense-in-depth that holds even if the docs drift again. | (a) Make the GATE re-derive caps from the raw manifest text (REJECTED: duplicates the parser, a second source of truth, I4 violation); (b) have the gate treat "empty caps + a body that mentions hosts" as pending (REJECTED: unbounded heuristic on untrusted body text, false-positive minefield, not a real boundary); (c) silently MOVE top-level caps under `capabilities` in the parser (REJECTED: silently rewriting an adversarial manifest is exactly the wrong instinct — fail loud, make the author re-draft). |
| 2026-05-30 | **Align the `skill_propose` tool description (`@ax/tool-skill-propose/descriptor.ts`) + the runner executor split-error wording TO the parser contract, never the reverse.** Canonical frontmatter: `name:` (lowercase slug, parser maps → `id`), integer `version` (not semver), capabilities nested under a `capabilities:` mapping. | The parser is the authoritative, security-bearing contract (it gates caps). The docs were the drifted artifact (TASK-74 wrote `id`+semver+top-level caps). Moving the docs to the parser keeps ONE documented contract; changing the parser to accept `id`/semver/top-level would weaken the validation surface. | Change the parser to accept `id` as an alias (REJECTED: two identity keys = ambiguity + a wider attack surface; `name` is already the established key across every other skill flow). |
| 2026-05-30 | **Boundary review: no hook-surface change.** The parser change is internal to `@ax/skills-parser` (a stricter branch of an existing reject path). The `skills:propose` hook payload and the `skill.propose` IPC schema are unchanged. No new/changed service-hook signature, no field-name leak, no new subscriber risk. | Required checklist; the change is a plugin-internal impl detail, so per CLAUDE.md it doesn't need full boundary review — noted for completeness. | — |

| 2026-05-30 | Lockfile recipe DIVERGES from TASK-65's "splice importer block only": this package adds a NEW third-party dep (@aws-sdk/client-s3) with a large transitive tree (@smithy/*, etc.) absent from the lockfile today, so new snapshot entries ARE required. Approach: targeted `pnpm add` of the exact-pinned dep in the new package, then verify `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is internally consistent and `pnpm audit --audit-level moderate` is clean (CI gate). KEY FINDING resolving the card's literal "make .bashrc add it" wording: the agent's runtime `$HOME` is **`/permanent`** (`agent-claude-sdk-runner/src/main.ts:735` `HOME: env.workspaceRoot`, default `/permanent` — env.ts:105), the git-bundled-and-restored workspace, NOT the image's `/home/axagent`. So `$HOME/bin` = `/permanent/bin`, exactly the persisted location. And the SDK Bash tool runs a **non-interactive** shell whose PATH comes ENTIRELY from the explicit `query({options:{env}})` allowlist (`proxy-startup.ts` forwards `process.env.PATH`; its comment: "Without forwarding PATH, the SDK's Bash tool executes `ls` and gets exit code 127" — proof no rc file is sourced, else a default PATH would exist). A plain `.bashrc` is interactive-only → the agent's shell would NOT source it. DECISION: do BOTH minimal layers — (a) the **Dockerfile** writes a `.bashrc` to the image home that adds `$HOME/bin` to PATH (satisfies the literal ask + covers any interactive/BASH_ENV shell + is the discoverable convention), and (b) the **load-bearing** fix: add `${env.workspaceRoot}/bin` to the forwarded `PATH` in `main.ts`'s SDK env literal so the non-interactive Bash tool actually sees `/permanent/bin`. **APPEND, not prepend (codex Phase-5 [P2], accepted):** `$HOME=/permanent` is model-WRITABLE + restored across sessions, so PREPENDING would let a prompt-injection/malicious-tool-output `/permanent/bin/git` (or node/python) PERSISTENTLY shadow the trusted image/venv binary in every future session — an I5/capability-minimization violation. Appending keeps installed tools discoverable (the goal) while trusted base+venv bins win on name collisions. (My original prepend rationale "the agent already controls its session" missed the cross-session PERSISTENCE + injection angle codex flagged.) Regression test: assert the SDK-subprocess PATH ENDS with `:<workspaceRoot>/bin` AND does NOT start with `<workspaceRoot>/bin:` (catches both a dropped-append regression and a re-introduced prepend) + a Dockerfile-content guard in `scripts/__tests__/dockerfile-home-bin-path.test.js` (runs unconditionally every PR via `pnpm test:scripts`, NOT package-affected-gated) asserting `.bashrc` carries `PATH="$PATH:$HOME/bin"` and NOT the prepend form. | Honors card INTENT (binaries found across sessions) via the mechanism that works for THIS runtime, not the one the card's wording assumes. `/permanent/bin` is the only dir that both is `$HOME/bin` AND persists (git-bundled); a binary in the image's `/home/axagent/bin` is neither writable by the agent's session nor where `$HOME` points. (b) is required because (a) alone is dead code for the SDK's non-interactive shell. | (a) ONLY the .bashrc, as the card's words say (rejected: the SDK Bash tool doesn't source .bashrc → the agent never gets it → half-wired/dead per the no-half-wired invariant); (b) ONLY mutate main.ts PATH, skip .bashrc (rejected: the card explicitly asks for the Dockerfile/.bashrc change + .bashrc is the human-discoverable convention for any future interactive shell); (c) set BASH_ENV in the forwarded env to point at a script (rejected: heavier, and the explicit-PATH forward is the established seam the venv/cache code already uses — mutate PATH the same way `buildPythonVenvEnv` does); (d) bake binaries into image `/home/axagent/bin` (rejected: misreads "persists between sessions" — that's the workspace tier, not the image) |

## 2026-05-25 — ARCH-11: shared golden-vectors drift test for MCP validators (no cross-import)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-05-25 |
| Decision | Detect drift between the runner's hand-rolled `validateMcpEntry` (`packages/agent-runner-core/src/installed-skills.ts`) and `@ax/sandbox-protocol`'s `McpServerSchema` via a single shared JSON fixture of golden vectors, asserted by TWO independent test suites — one in each package — both reading the same fixture file. A divergence (one validator accepts what the other rejects) fails one suite → CI red. |
| Rationale | The CRITICAL INVARIANT (and the ARCH-5 design intent) is that the runner stays independent of the host contract package: NO `@ax/sandbox-protocol` import (not even devDependency) in the runner, so the sandbox-side re-validation is genuine defense-in-depth, not a thin wrapper. A shared JSON fixture is data, not code — neither package imports the other. Each side reads the fixture via `join(__dirname,'..','..','..','..',<path>)` (the idiomatic worktree-safe repo-root pattern from cli/e2e.test.ts), then maps its own validator over the vectors. |
| Alternatives | (a) Have the runner import McpServerSchema and delegate — REJECTED, destroys the independence that is the whole point. (b) Cross-reference comment only — REJECTED by dispatch: a comment doesn't *detect* drift. (c) Put the drift test in one package importing the other's validator — REJECTED: sandbox-protocol is a pure zod package, pulling in the runner (with its SDK dep) reverses+bloats the dep graph; and importing the schema into the runner-side test re-creates the forbidden coupling. Two-sided fixture is the only shape with zero cross-import. |
| Fixture home | `packages/sandbox-protocol/src/__tests__/fixtures/mcp-server-golden-vectors.json` — sandbox-protocol OWNS the canonical schema, so the canonical vectors live with it. The runner-side test reaches it read-only via repo-root-relative path (no package dep). |
| Scope of vectors | Only the security-relevant fields BOTH validators enforce: name regex, transport enum, command presence/non-empty, args max(32)/len(256), env Record<string,string> shape + size caps, url validity, and the stdio/http transport refine (cross-contamination). EXCLUDED: cases hinging purely on `allowedHosts`/`credentials` — the runner intentionally ignores those (it only emits name/transport/command/args/env/url into .mcp.json), so they are a KNOWN, documented benign divergence, not drift. Each vector is normalized to drop allowedHosts/credentials before the runner sees it, OR the runner-side harness ignores them (the runner already does). |
| Known benign divergence | runner `validateMcpEntry` does not look at `allowedHosts`/`credentials`; `McpServerSchema` defaults+validates them. Documented inline in both the fixture header and a cross-reference comment on `validateMcpEntry`. |

### 2026-05-25 — ARCH-11 follow-on: assertion SEMANTICS (runner may be stricter; symmetric on the security-critical core)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Decision | Each golden vector declares its expected verdict per side: `schema: 'accept'|'reject'` and `runner: 'accept'|'reject'`. The test asserts BOTH sides match their declared verdict. This models the legitimate asymmetry (runner = defense-in-depth, allowed to be a strict-superset rejecter) WITHOUT letting silent drift hide: any future change to either validator that flips a verdict breaks the test, forcing a conscious fixture update + cross-reference review. A `sameVerdict` invariant subset (the security-critical shape rules: name regex, transport enum, transport refine, command presence, url validity, args caps) is additionally asserted to be IDENTICAL on both sides — those MUST never diverge; only the env entry-count/length caps are runner-stricter-by-design. |
| Rationale | Found a real today-divergence: runner caps env to ≤32 entries and ≤256-char keys/values; `McpServerSchema` (`z.record(z.string(), z.string())`) caps neither. The dangerous direction is "schema accepts, runner accepts, but it's malicious" — the runner is the LAST gate, so runner-stricter is the safe direction and must be allowed. The unsafe direction is "schema rejects but runner accepts" (a hole past the last gate) — vectors with `schema:'reject', runner:'accept'` are the ones we never want to exist; the test would surface any. |
| Decision on the env-cap gap | Do NOT "fix" it by loosening the runner or tightening the schema in THIS card (scope = drift DETECTION, per dispatch). Encode the current reality in the vectors (env-oversize: `schema:'accept', runner:'reject'`) + a documented note, and return "tighten McpServerSchema env caps to match runner (≤32 entries, ≤256 key/val)" as a deferred follow-up for auto-ship to file. Tightening the schema is the right eventual fix (host should reject early) but it changes the host contract + needs its own boundary review. |
| Human-owned? | No — resolvable from code + the documented defense-in-depth design intent. Not escalating. |
