Env-hints are inert strings, change zero capabilities, and `TERM`/`COLUMNS`/`LINES` are ALREADY in proxy-startup ENV_ALLOWLIST (just never set in the detached host), so the precedent is set. → pty TAKEN OFF THE TABLE. | (a) pseudo-TTY for the Bash child (rejected: significant sandbox-boundary cost per above, and env-hints suffice for the targeted class); (b) only FORCE_COLOR (rejected: color isn't the gate — the tool emits NOTHING incl plain --help; need TERM+size+CI too); (c) document the limitation only (rejected: card's desired outcome is a CODE FIX that makes tools emit, plus a compat note — not docs-only) |
| 2026-05-25 | TASK-26: helper lives in the RUNNER (`@ax/agent-runner-core/tty-hint-env.ts`, moved there by #395), spread into the single SDK env literal in main.ts — NOT in the per-backend sandbox env (sandbox-subprocess open-session.ts / sandbox-k8s pod-spec.ts). | One source of truth (I4): both sandbox backends funnel their session env into the runner, which then builds the SINGLE `query({options:{env}})` env the SDK Bash tool actually inherits (proven by home-bin-env.ts / tool-cache-env.ts living there for exactly this reason — the Bash tool is a non-interactive shell that gets PATH only from this literal, no rc sourced). Putting hints in both pod-spec + open-session would duplicate + risk drift; putting them in the runner covers BOTH backends with one edit and matches the existing buildHomeBinEnv/buildToolCacheEnv pattern. SPREAD FIRST (before anthropicEnv) so a genuinely-forwarded TERM/COLUMNS (if the host ever has a TTY) overrides the default — defaults are a floor, not a clamp. | (a) set in sandbox-subprocess + sandbox-k8s env (rejected: two edits, drift risk, and those envs feed the RUNNER process not the SDK Bash child directly — the runner rebuilds the SDK env from an allowlist, so a TERM set on the runner only reaches the Bash child if it's in ENV_ALLOWLIST AND set, which is the current gap); (b) add FORCE_COLOR/CI to proxy-startup ENV_ALLOWLIST + set them on the sandbox env (rejected: same two-place + allowlist-coupling problem; the runner env literal is the clean single seam) |

## 2026-05-25 — TASK-24: Host OOMKill mid-turn silently loses the turn

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-25 | **Root cause (3 cascade points):** (1) the runner's IPC client (`ipc-client.ts`) retries transient errnos (incl ECONNREFUSED) only `maxRetries=5` with 100→30s-cap backoff = ~3.1s total, far shorter than a host OOMKill+pod-reschedule+boot. (2) After the budget exhausts, `commitNotifyWithResync` catches the throw → `kept` → turn never committed → `conversations:get` = 0 turns. (3) The NEXT `inbox.next()` (`session.next-message` long-poll) also throws the terminal `HostUnavailableError` → propagates to `userMessages()` → out of SDK `query()` → top-level catch → `exitCode=1` → `terminated`. Both the logged "commit-notify failed" AND the exit-1 are the same too-short retry budget. | The report attributed it to commit-notify alone, but the exit-1 is the inbox poll. Fixing only commit-notify would still crash the runner on the next poll. | — |
| 2026-05-25 | **#1 commit-notify resilience: lengthen the IPC client's transient-error retry budget to ~2min (TASK clarification: 2min max), retry/backoff (NOT buffer-and-replay).** Add a per-call `maxElapsedMs` deadline to `ipc-client.ts withRetry` so transient/5xx retries keep going (backoff capped at 30s) until ~120s elapsed, then throw. This single change fixes BOTH the commit-notify drop AND the inbox-poll runner crash, because both go through the same client retry loop. A host OOMKill+restart on kind completes well within 2min, so the turn commits and the poll reconnects — runner survives, turn persists. | retry/backoff chosen over buffer-and-replay: the IPC client already has a retry loop; adding a wall-clock deadline is a ~10-line surgical change vs. a whole disk-spool buffer subsystem. Buffer-and-replay would also need idempotency on the host commit-notify (it has it via parentVersion, but spooling adds complexity for no UX gain — the user is already waiting on the turn). The 2min bound caps how long a genuinely-dead host hangs the user. | buffer-and-replay (rejected: heavier, no UX win); raise only maxRetries count (rejected: count is a poor proxy for wall-clock; a wall-clock deadline is the right knob for "survive a restart"). |
| 2026-05-25 | **#2 recovery UX: auto-retry the whole turn + show a "session interrupted, retrying" message.** TASK clarification mandates auto-retry (vs FAULTA-5's deliberate manual-retry-only stance). This case differs from FAULTA-5's: here the turn produced **0 committed turns** (nothing persisted, no partial replay hazard) — so auto-retrying the whole turn is loss-free and duplicate-free (the server-side history is empty for this turn; `session:terminate` already cleared `active_session_id` so the retry routes to a fresh sandbox). Implement in channel-web transport/runtime: on the CONNECTION_LOST / sandbox-terminated path, auto-invoke `regenerate()` ONCE with an interim "Session interrupted — retrying…" status, falling back to the manual-retry banner if the auto-retry also fails. | FAULTA-5's manual-only stance was about mid-stream connection-lost where the server turn was LIVE (duplicate side-effect risk). TASK-24's OOMKill case = turn fully lost, host restarted, fresh sandbox on retry → safe to auto-retry. Bounded to ONE auto-retry so a persistently-dead host doesn't loop forever; then manual banner. | keep manual-only (rejected: TASK clarification explicitly wants auto-retry + message); unbounded auto-retry (rejected: infinite loop on a hard-down host). |
| 2026-05-25 | **#3a memory: raise host limit 512Mi→2048Mi in kind-dev-values.yaml** (TASK clarification). Bump request 128Mi→256Mi to keep the request/limit ratio sane for the scheduler. | Per TASK clarification. 512Mi was tipped over by one heavy proxy-MITM turn atop the orchestrator. | — |
| 2026-05-25 | **#3b proxy buffering caps: (a) cap the plain-HTTP request-body buffer in `handleHTTPRequest` (currently UNBOUNDED `Buffer.concat`) at 16 MiB → 413; (b) add write-backpressure on both MITM data pumps (`clientTls.write`/`targetTls.write` ignore the bool return → unbounded socket buffer on a slow consumer) by pausing the source socket when write() returns false and resuming on 'drain'.** Builder's-recommendation cap = 16 MiB request body (generous for any legit upload; a multi-GB upload OOMs the 512Mi/2048Mi host otherwise). | The report's case is an HTTPS-MITM *download* (response) — the response side already streams chunk-by-chunk but WITHOUT honoring write backpressure, so a slow runner-pod consumer lets chunks pile in the host's socket buffers unbounded. Backpressure is the real per-request buffering cap for the MITM download path. The plain-HTTP request-body concat is a separate unbounded vector worth capping in the same PR. | cap response body size (rejected: a legit large download should succeed, just not OOM — backpressure bounds memory without capping size); leave plain-HTTP unbounded (rejected: it's a live OOM vector). |

- `2026-05-26` (TASK-33) | Followed the locked impl plan `docs/plans/2026-05-26-jit-per-user-skill-attachment-orchestrator-union-impl.md` verbatim after verifying every code anchor against worktree HEAD (zero drift). | The card says "decisions locked (design §4 + Appendix); implementation-only" and the plan ships real code for every step. Verifying anchors first (per receiving-code-review discipline) confirmed the orchestrator's exact 1045-1046 anchor, the `buildSkillsHooks`/`buildProxyHooks` test helpers, `TEST_AGENT.id='test-agent'`/userId='test-user', and the canary capture harness — so no re-derivation needed. | Alt: re-brainstorm scope — rejected, card is implementation-only and the plan's Self-Review already covers spec/placeholder/type/stale-anchor checks.

## 2026-05-26 — TASK-44: persist grant is best-effort (don't 500 a successful live grant)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Decision | In `routes-allow-host.ts`, wrap the `host-grants:grant` persist call in try/catch (log `host_grant_persist_failed` + swallow). A persist failure returns `{ added }` 200, not 500. |
| Rationale | The LIVE `proxy:add-host` widen already succeeded before the persist attempt, so the host works for the current session. A persist-only failure (grant-limit at the 256 cap, or a transient DB blip) shouldn't surface as a request error — it would confuse the user (the host IS live) and the only loss is durability, which the user recovers by re-hitting the wall next fresh spawn. Same fail-direction as the orchestrator's fail-open load: a failure yields fewer persisted hosts, never more, so it can't widen egress. Found in the `/code-review --effort high` substitute pass (Codex was usage-limited this session). |
| Alternatives | (a) Let it propagate → 500 on cap/DB-blip even though the live grant worked (rejected: bad UX, dishonest about the live state). (b) Map `grant-limit` → a specific 4xx (rejected: still fails a successful live grant; the persist is genuinely secondary). |

- `2026-05-30` (TASK-86) — **Per-skill credential-slot namespacing fixes the skill-slot-collision LOCKOUT (two active authored skills sharing a slot like LINEAR_API_KEY terminated EVERY chat turn).** Chosen approach (a, human-decided in card Clarifications; (b) relevant-only-union rejected): namespace SKILL slots `skill:<id>:<slot>` in the host-side credentials map handed to `proxy:open-session`, keep AGENT/trusted base creds (`agent.requiredCredentials` / Anthropic default) BARE. Two skills' same-named slots → two distinct namespaced keys → two distinct `ax-cred:<hex>` placeholders → no collision. Skill-vs-agent collision is NO LONGER fatal: the trusted bare credential always WINS the flat sandbox env stamp; a skill's namespaced cred still exists in the proxy map for its own egress but can't hijack the trusted env var (old security guarantee preserved as a benign no-op suppression, not a lockout). KEY ARCH FACT making the bare-env requirement satisfiable: proxy substitution is VALUE-based (`registry.ts replaceAll` replaces `ax-cred:<hex>` wherever it appears, regardless of env-var name), so the env-var NAME is just a placeholder vehicle — the orchestrator projects the namespaced `envMap` BACK to bare env names (`projectEnvMapToBareNames`, trusted-wins + deterministic skill precedence) before threading into `proxyConfig.envMap` (the flat sandbox env). Skills share ONE flat sandbox env (no per-skill process/env scope), so two skills sharing a bare slot name still collapse to ONE value in the flat env (precedence wins) — IRREDUCIBLE; the win is no-lockout + each cred reaching the proxy independently. git-cred wiring (`buildGitCredentialEnv` @ax/sandbox-protocol) must use each skill's OWN placeholder (threaded as optional `credentials[].placeholder` on InstalledSkillSchema, back-compat falls back to `envMap[slot]`) so per-skill git egress stays correct even when the flat-env stamp went to the other skill. Also in scope (card Clarifications): (T4) tuned `CRED_EXFIL` scanner so benign `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $X_API_KEY"` against an allowed host stops false-tripping `credential-exfiltration`; (T5) scoped the pending cap-skill JIT "Connect…" card to its PROPOSING conversation (in-memory `pendingSkillConversation: Map<skillId,conversationId>` set in `onSkillsProposed`, same single-replica posture as respawnSessions/upfrontCardsByConv) so it stops persisting across unrelated conversations.

- `2026-05-31` (TASK-88) — **SSE-open retry extended from TASK-84's fixed ~1.45s (4-attempt) budget to a wall-clock ~30s budget of capped-exponential backoff (250ms doubling, cap 2s) so a cold-respawn 404 auto-recovers — no manual Retry click.** Client-only, `packages/channel-web/src/lib/transport.ts` `openSseStream`. Replaced the counted loop with an open-ended `for(;;)` gated on a `Date.now()+SSE_OPEN_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS` deadline (each retry wait clamped to the remaining budget). Decided budget=30s (card said ~20-30s): a cold kind runner pod spawn + per-reqId bind takes ~5-15s, 30s gives margin; bounded so a turn that died before ANY bind still terminates → banner. SAFE per the card's key insight + FAULTA-5 history: the GET only replays a bounded per-reqId buffer (chunk-buffer.ts) and never starts a turn (only POST does), so re-opening it far longer than 1.45s can't duplicate a turn — unlike a `regenerate()` re-POST, which FAULTA-5 (decisions 2026-05-25) forbids automating. Retryable set unchanged (404/425/429/5xx + network throw); 401/403/400/413 fail fast on attempt 1 (card: "unchanged"). **Review-fix decision:** the terminal throw now differs by reason — a spent budget on a RETRYABLE failure throws `new Error(CONNECTION_LOST)` (the FAULTA-5 sentinel) so the runtime's `onError`→`applyTurnError` shows the user-facing "Connection lost. Retry to continue." banner + manual-retry button (the card's "fall back to the existing CONNECTION_LOST banner"); a fail-fast NON-retryable status keeps its verbatim `chat-flow SSE open failed: <status>` (a real client error is not a connection loss). TASK-84 had thrown the raw status string on ALL terminal exits — that pre-existing gap missed the card's acceptance, so I fixed it with a `failFast` flag set only on the non-retryable break. During the wait surface `agentStatusActions.show(PHASE_LABELS['sandbox-starting'])` ("Starting sandbox…") set LAZILY (only after the first retryable failure) so the happy-path first-open never flashes it. OUT OF SCOPE (handoff follow-up): harden the server early-bind to be authoritative (retry the bind / 503 the POST) so `active_req_id` is guaranteed before the 202. | Rationale: budget-driven (not attempt-count) is self-documenting and decouples the cold-boot window from the backoff curve; CONNECTION_LOST fallback honors the card acceptance + reuses the established sentinel/wording rather than inventing new copy; lazy status avoids a flash on the common warm-path. | Alternatives: (a) keep an attempt count, just bump it (rejected — couples timing to count, harder to reason about a "~30s" budget); (b) throw raw status on budget exhaustion like TASK-84 (rejected — misses the card's "surfaces CONNECTION_LOST" acceptance + shows dev-ish copy to users); (c) show CONNECTION_LOST for the 403 fail-fast too (rejected — a 403 is a real auth error, not a connection loss; "unchanged" per card); (d) eagerly set "Starting sandbox…" before the first open (rejected — flashes on every warm turn).

- `2026-05-31` (TASK-90, epic connectors-first-class) — **The capability shape now has a NEUTRAL canonical name: `Capabilities` in `@ax/skills-parser` (`packages/skills-parser/src/capabilities.ts`); `SkillCapabilities` is a back-compat `export type` alias of it.** Pure type/export-only refactor, no behavior/hook/table change. Why: per the connectors-first-class design a future connector object references the SAME `allowedHosts`/`credentials`/`mcpServers`/`packages` shape, and CLAUDE.md invariant #2 forbids a cross-plugin import — so the shared shape must live under a neutral name in the dependency-free `@ax/skills-parser` (already eslint-allowlisted for both `@ax/skills` and `@ax/agents`). The sub-types (`CapabilitySlot`/`McpServerSpec`/`PackagesSpec`) were ALREADY neutral-named — only the top-level interface needed renaming. `index.ts` now re-exports `Capabilities` + `PackagesSpec` (previously unexported) alongside the existing names. Migrated the two INTERNAL `src` consumers (`manifest.ts` `ParsedManifest.capabilities`, `build.ts` input) to the neutral name so `pnpm build` (tsc) is the load-bearing regression guard — PROVEN: renaming the export away makes the build go red. External consumers (`@ax/skills`, `@ax/agents`, `@ax/skill-broker`) were left on the `SkillCapabilities` alias (zero churn, alias keeps them compiling). | Rationale: smallest honest diff that satisfies the card + makes the neutral name real and guarded; test files aren't type-checked anywhere in this repo's gate (build excludes `__tests__`, vitest strips types, eslint isn't type-aware) so a type-only test CAN'T be the guard — a migrated `src` consumer is. | Alternatives: (a) mass-rewrite every consumer to `Capabilities` (rejected — needless churn, the card says "Skills continue to consume the type exactly as before"); (b) add a runtime sentinel value to make the vitest test load-bearing (rejected — adds unrequested runtime API, YAGNI); (c) leave both `src` consumers on the alias and rely only on the (unchecked) vitest test (rejected — then nothing in the gate guards the neutral export).

Check `git fetch origin main` + diff the shared files BEFORE assuming your base is current; auto-ship merges siblings ahead of you.** Also: `connectors:resolve` does NOT carry `usageNote` (it's the routing descriptor); only `connectors:list-defaults` (full Connector) does — private connectors resolved via resolve fall back to a generic synthetic SKILL.md body (acceptable; the note is a nicety, not load-bearing for reach).

## 2026-05-31 | TASK-95 scope: full connector-authoring chain, not just SKILL.md
- **Decision:** TASK-95 builds the FULL connector-authoring chain — a `connector_propose` model-facing tool (descriptor + sandbox executor + IPC action `connector.install-authored` → host hook `connectors:install-authored`) PLUS the `ax-connector-creator` builtin SKILL.md PLUS narrowing `ax-skill-creator` to know-how. Not just the SKILL.md the card's Acceptance lists.

The host hook `connectors:install-authored` is registered but has NO model-facing caller. A SKILL.md telling the agent to call a tool that doesn't exist is a half-wired skill (invariant #3). No other board card (TASK-96..100) owns the executor/IPC. Design §"Authoring" line 180 defines the loop as calling install_authored_connector → so the tool must exist.
- **Alternatives:** (a) ship only the SKILL.md per the card's literal Acceptance — rejected: half-wired, references a non-existent tool. (b) block for human scope call — rejected: the scope is unambiguously resolvable from TASK-94's handoff + the design; not a product decision.
- **GOTCHA found:** the current `ax-skill-creator` SKILL.md is ALREADY STALE — it teaches `install_authored_skill({skillId,hosts,slots,packages})` + `.ax/draft-skills/`, but that tool was DELETED (commit 4d3d0bc8) and replaced by `skill_propose({path})` writing to `/ephemeral/skill-draft/<id>/` with a `capabilities:` block IN frontmatter (TASK-74). The live runner system-prompt (skillAuthoringNote) uses skill_propose. Narrowing ax-skill-creator must also fix it to the skill_propose reality.

## 2026-05-31 | TASK-95 architecture: host-executed connector_propose tool (NOT a sandbox executor + IPC chain)
- **Decision:** The model-facing connector-authoring tool is `connector_propose`, a HOST-executed tool (`executesIn: 'host'`) in a new package `@ax/tool-connector-propose` — mirroring `@ax/skill-broker`'s `request_capability`, NOT `@ax/tool-skill-propose`'s sandbox-executor+IPC pattern. It registers BOTH the descriptor (tool:register) AND `tool:execute:connector_propose`, reads (userId, agentId) from the host-trusted tool ctx, and calls the existing `connectors:install-authored` hook on the bus.
- **Rationale:** connector args are pure structured JSON `{connectorId,name,hosts,slots,packages,mcpServers,usageNote,keyMode}` the model produces inline — there is NO draft directory to read from the sandbox FS (unlike skill_propose which must read /ephemeral/skill-draft/<id>/). So the sandbox-executor + IPC-action chain TASK-94's note sketched is UNNECESSARY complexity; the request_capability host-tool shape is the right, smaller fit. The host hook `connectors:install-authored` is the authoritative validator (I5 trust boundary); the tool is a thin scope-stamping adapter (light shape check + clean error map, like request_capability's skillId check).
- **Alternatives:** (a) sandbox executor + connector.install-authored IPC action (TASK-94's literal sketch) — rejected: no FS bytes to read sandbox-side; pure overhead. (b) add connector_propose into @ax/skill-broker — rejected: broker's identity is skill-CATALOG brokering (hard calls skills:*); a new package per authoring tool matches the @ax/tool-skill-propose convention and keeps the connectors:install-authored dep isolated + hasService-gated.
- New package needs project refs in root tsconfig.json AND presets/k8s/tsconfig.json (TASK-91 gotcha) + an entry in ALWAYS_ON_BROKER_TOOLS so non-wildcard agents see it.

## 2026-06-03 — TASK-147: decouple admin identity save from the tools-required gate (wildcard/bare agents)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-06-03 | The AgentForm tools-required gate fires only when the save would CREATE a new wildcard agent or DEMOTE a tool-listed agent to wildcard — never on a bare-stays-bare identity edit. On such an edit the PATCH OMITS `allowedTools`+`mcpConfigIds`. | TASK-143 walk GLITCH: the combined AgentForm Save was over-gated — its unconditional `if (allowedTools.length===0) return` aborted the whole submit (incl. `putAgentIdentity`) for an existing wildcard/bare agent. The standalone `PUT /admin/agents/:id/identity` route is ungated and worked. A bare agent (`allowedTools=[]`) is a legit store-allowed state; the server only rejects the wildcard sentinel when BOTH `allowedTools` AND `mcpConfigIds` are present-and-empty (`rejectsWildcardScope`, agents/admin-routes.ts), on create AND update. So omitting both empty fields from the PATCH leaves the agent bare and avoids the server rejection. | (a) Suppress the gate globally — rejected: would let the form create new wildcard agents, which the server (correctly) rejects, and let a tool-listed agent be silently demoted. (b) Always send `allowedTools:[]` on the bare edit — rejected: server `rejectsWildcardScope` 400s on the both-empty PATCH. |

Key facts learned (server-side wildcard rule, `packages/agents/src/admin-routes.ts`):
- `rejectsWildcardScope` triggers ONLY when `allowedTools` AND `mcpConfigIds` are both present-and-empty; runs on both `create` and `update`.
- `updateBodySchema` makes every field optional → a PATCH that omits the tool fields is accepted and leaves the agent's tool scope untouched.

| 2026-06-03 | The connector approval card now surfaces the instant the agent proposes a connector (mid-turn), not only at the start of the user's NEXT turn. `@ax/connectors` `install-authored` fires a new `connectors:proposed` subscriber event after a successful PENDING upsert (NOT on the TASK-114 already-active no-op); `@ax/chat-orchestrator` subscribes (`onConnectorProposed`) and calls the EXISTING `fireUpfrontConnectorCards(ctx, ctx.agentId)` — the IPC-stamped `conversationId` matches the open turn's SSE so the card delivers live. Mirrors `skills:proposed`→`onSkillsProposed` and the skill JIT card (`request_capability` fires `chat:permission-request` mid-turn). Per-conversation dedup (`upfrontConnectorCardsByConv`) prevents a duplicate next turn. | BUG (found 2026-06-03 on kind): `fireUpfrontConnectorCards` was called ONLY at the two `agent:invoke` turn-start sites (warm-route + fresh-spawn). A connector proposed mid-turn-1 was never carded until turn-2; a user who proposed one and never sent a 2nd message had a stranded `pending` draft — invisible in chat AND in Settings (pending drafts aren't promoted to the live registry until approval). The grant boundary is unchanged: firing the card earlier grants nothing (draft stays zero-reach until explicit human approval; `shown` TOCTOU guard still applies). | (a) turn-end re-scan / per-turn poll of `connectors:list-authored` — rejected (the event mirrors skills:proposed exactly, one source of truth). (b) just fix the agent's "card is up" messaging — rejected (fragile, model-dependent; the card genuinely wasn't up). |
| 2026-06-03 | Settings → Connectors gains a "Proposed by your assistant" shelf so a missed/dismissed card isn't a dead end. New `connectors:list-authored-pending` hook + `store.listPendingForUser(userId)` (owner-scoped via new `scopedAuthoredConnectorsByUser`, status=pending, registry-excluded) aggregate the user's pending drafts ACROSS agents (each carries its `agentId`). User routes `GET /settings/connectors/authored` (list) + `POST /settings/connectors/authored/:id/approve` (`{agentId, shown?}` → `agents:resolve` ACL gate → `agent:apply-authored-connector-grant` with **conversationId omitted** = the approve-ahead path). channel-web `ProposedConnectorApproveDialog` is the in-chat card's twin (write key to vault → approve). | Pending authored drafts live in `connectors_v1_authored` and are only promoted into the live `connectors_v1_connectors` registry on approval (invariant #4 — registry is the one source of truth for active connectors; authored table is draft staging). Settings reads only the live registry, so before this a pending draft had NO approval surface other than the next-turn card. The approve-ahead grant path (optional `conversationId`) already existed for the My-Skills early-approve case; reused here. | List per selected-agent via the existing agent picker — rejected (user shouldn't have to know which agent proposed it; aggregate by owner instead). |

Walked end-to-end on `ax-next-dev` (branch image): Part A — "Connect Acme Test" card appeared on the proposing turn; Part B — dismissed card, Settings shelf showed it, Approve promoted it to Connected/Ready (draft→active + registry row + creds, DB-verified). Test artifacts cleaned up. Code lives in `@ax/connectors` (plugin.ts/authored-store.ts/scope.ts/types.ts/admin-routes.ts), `@ax/chat-orchestrator` (orchestrator.ts/plugin.ts), `@ax/channel-web` (lib/connectors.ts, settings/ConnectorsTab.tsx, settings/ProposedConnectorApproveDialog.tsx).

## 2026-06-03 — Dev-dependency services in the sandbox (Option A "compose-as-a-pod") — impl plan

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-03-dev-services-in-sandbox-impl.md` (decomposed into PR-sized
slices S1–S7 for auto-ship). Decision memo (WHY + spike evidence):
`docs/plans/2026-06-03-dev-services-in-sandbox-decision.md`.

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|------|----------|-----------|--------------|
| 2026-06-03 | Provide Kafka+Mongo to an agent's test run as **native sidecars in the runner pod** (`initContainers` + `restartPolicy: Always`), reachable at `localhost`. NOT plain `containers[]`. | Plain `containers[]` deadlock `watchPodExit` (`lifecycle.ts:192`): `restartPolicy:Never` (`pod-spec.ts:410`) makes the pod terminal only when ALL containers exit; the DBs never exit → pod leaks 6h. Native sidecars get SIGTERM'd on runner exit → pod Succeeds ~4s, and stay in `initContainerStatuses` so `containerStatuses[0]`=runner (exit-code logic untouched). | Sibling dev-services pod + egress hole (Option B — defeats the egress model); processes-in-runner (Option C — bloats trusted image); external services + TCP egress (Option D — no cred injection, breaks test isolation). |
| 2026-06-03 | gVisor stays ON → **JVM Kafka (KRaft) + Mongo**, NOT Redpanda. | Spike (GKE Autopilot/gVisor): Redpanda is control-proven gVisor-incompatible (early `open()` of a pseudo-file gVisor's stubbed /proc//sys doesn't expose; byte-identical pod boots fine on a normal node). Mongo + JVM Kafka both pass under gVisor. Pay the JVM cost to keep the untrusted runner sandboxed. | gVisor OFF for the pod (Redpanda works) — rejected: can't mix runtimes per-container, so it un-sandboxes the runner too. |
| 2026-06-03 | The `services` capability is a NEW field on the shared **`Capabilities`** shape (`@ax/skills-parser`), declared on **CONNECTORS**, folded via `connector-union.ts` — NOT on skills. | **Plan-vs-reality correction:** the decision memo + handoff prompt say "skill capability," but TASK-100 (2026-06-01) REMOVED the capability block from skill manifests — `skills-parser/manifest.ts` rejects any `capabilities:` key ("capabilities live on connectors now"). Connectors are the capability consumer; skills only NAME connectors. | **Operator-confirmed 2026-06-03: connectors, not agent-level — the agent path would force net-new image-allowlist governance the connector approval wall gives for free; an agent already attaches connectors so per-agent scoping is kept.** | Put it on the agent record — deferred; connectors already carry hosts/creds/mcp/packages and have the admin-approval wall + the `connector-union` fold path. |
| 2026-06-03 | Descriptor = `{ name, image(@sha256-pinned), ports, env, healthcheck, writablePaths }` on `OpenSessionInputSchema`; NO `pod`/`container`/`securityContext`/`runtimeClassName`/`volume`/`emptyDir`/`initContainers` vocabulary (I1/invariant#1). Each backend translates. | Transport/storage-agnostic hook surface. `writablePaths` (not `emptyDirs`) → k8s emptyDir mounts; `healthcheck:{kind:'tcp'|'exec'}` (not k8s `readinessProbe`) → backend-mapped. | — |
| 2026-06-03 | **S1 (credential-proxy hostPath → TCP-listen + Service + CA-without-hostPath) is the production-gVisor root.** | GKE Sandbox bans `hostPath`; today the proxy socket is shared via a hostPath mount. Proxy already supports `listen:{kind:'tcp'}`; work = chart Service + NetworkPolicy egress (runner→proxy-Service) + delivering `caCertPem` to the runner via env (`AX_PROXY_CA_PEM`, written to tmpfs at boot — mirrors the subprocess backend) instead of a shared dir. | — |
| 2026-06-03 | Defaults stated (not blocked): per-session services (clean state); digest-pinned + admin-allowlisted images; a team `docker-compose.yml` is TRANSLATED as curated input (drop host mounts/`privileged`/`cap_add`/host-net/socket mounts), never auto-imported. | Untrusted compose must not cross into the trusted pod verbatim. | — |

**Slice DAG:** S1 (proxy TCP, root) ∥ S2 (descriptor+grammar+validator, OPENS half-wired
window) → S3 (k8s sidecars) ∥ S4 (subprocess docker-compose) → S5 (orchestrator fold) →
S6 (declare UI + compose translate) ∥ S7 (canary, CLOSES window + `(walk)` kind walk).
Deps: S3←S2, S4←S2, S5←S2,S3,S4, S6←S2,S5, S7←S3,S4,S5.

**Spike artifacts (don't redo):** verdict table in the decision memo; throwaway script
`~/spike-1b-gke-gvisor.sh` (up/test/norc/kafka/down). gVisor proof was GKE Autopilot
(`runtimeClassName: gvisor` alone auto-provisions a `sandbox=gvisor` node — no nodepool/taint).

## 2026-06-03 — Dev-services slices: TASK-149 (proxy TCP) + TASK-151 (k8s sidecars) — implementation decisions

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-03 | TASK-151 (k8s native-sidecar rendering). The per-session readiness BUDGET (which scales with service count) is computed by a pure `computeReadinessBudgetMs({ baseTimeoutMs, serviceCount, perServiceColdStartMs })` exported from `@ax/sandbox-k8s/config.ts`, called in `open-session.ts` step 4 where `input.services.length` is in scope — NOT baked into `ResolvedSandboxK8sConfig.readinessTimeoutMs` (that stays the service-LESS 60s default). Formula: `serviceCount === 0 ? baseTimeoutMs : baseTimeoutMs + serviceCount * perServiceColdStartMs`. New config fields: `serviceCpuLimit`/`serviceMemoryLimit`/`serviceCpuRequest`/`serviceMemoryRequest` (per-sidecar resourcing) + `perServiceColdStartMs` (default 120_000 — JVM cold-start + image pull + sequential gate). | Card pins the policy to config.ts but the budget VALUE is per-session (service count is a request quantity, not a config constant). A pure fn keeps the policy constants in config while the count multiplies at the call site. Baking a fixed timeout into the resolved config would lose the "scales with N" requirement. | (a) compute inside config.resolveConfig — rejected, resolveConfig has no service count. (b) inline the formula in open-session — rejected, the constants belong with the other config defaults + a pure fn is unit-testable. |
| 2026-06-03 | TASK-151 per-`writablePaths` emptyDir volume naming: `svc-<serviceName>-<i>` where i is the writablePaths index. serviceName already matches ID_RE (lowercase alnum + dashes, k8s-name-safe); the index disambiguates a service's multiple writable paths and prevents collisions across services. Each volume is `{ name, emptyDir: {} }`; the matching sidecar volumeMount is `{ name, mountPath: <writablePath> }`. | DNS-1123 + ≤63-char k8s volume-name rules + uniqueness across N services × M paths. ID_RE-constrained name keeps it valid without sanitization; index keeps it unique. | Hashing the path — rejected (opaque in `kubectl describe`, and ID_RE name + index is already collision-free). |
| 2026-06-03 | TASK-151 sidecar env: stamp ONLY the descriptor's own `env` map. Sidecars get NEITHER the runner's git-paranoid/proxy/CA env NOR AX_* — they're third-party service images, not the runner. The egress lock (I4) is enforced at the NetworkPolicy layer (S1), not via env; services bind 0.0.0.0 by their own image default, the descriptor never encodes a bind address. startupProbe comes from `healthcheck` ({kind:'tcp',port}→tcpSocket; {kind:'exec',command}→exec); omitted when healthcheck absent. ports→containerPort. Locked containerSecurity reused verbatim (runAsNonRoot/uid+gid 1000/caps drop ALL/readOnlyRootFilesystem). | I5 (minimize capabilities) + I1 (backend-agnostic descriptor). A leaked AX_AUTH_TOKEN or proxy CA on a third-party sidecar would widen blast radius for no benefit. | Inheriting runner env "for convenience" — rejected, it's a capability leak onto an untrusted-adjacent container. |
| 2026-06-03 | TASK-151 review finding (self-caught, fixed in-branch): k8s container + volume NAMES are DNS-1123 labels capped at 63 BYTES, a DIFFERENT constraint from the session-id LABEL VALUE that `sanitizeLabel` already handles. `ServiceDescriptorSchema`'s `ID_RE` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`) permits a 64-char service name, so a naive `svc-<name>` (and `svc-<name>-<i>` volume name) overflows → the API server rejects the WHOLE pod with an opaque 422 → session roll-back. Added `serviceNameBase()` in pod-spec.ts: deterministic truncate-+-sha1-suffix when `svc-<name>` plus a 3-byte index reserve would exceed 63; short names (postgres/kafka/mongo) pass through unchanged. | When rendering any k8s resource name (container/volume/label-KEY ≤63) from a schema-permitted string whose max length can exceed the k8s limit, bound it deterministically. ID_RE's `{0,63}` quantifier means MAX 64 chars (1 anchor + 63), not 63 — easy off-by-one to miss. | Reuse `sanitizeLabel` — rejected, it sanitizes label VALUES (different char rules, no `svc-`/index-reserve awareness); a focused helper is clearer. |

| 2026-06-03 | **TASK-149: TCP-mode discriminator for the credential-proxy is `config.proxySocketHostPath` EMPTY + `proxyConfig.endpoint` set; hostPath-mode is `proxySocketHostPath` non-empty.** The credential-proxy plugin ALREADY supports `listen: { kind: 'tcp', host, port }` and `buildEndpointString` already emits `tcp://host:port` — the gap was never the listener, it's (a) the advertised cluster Service URL (bind host ≠ reachable host) and (b) CA delivery without a shared dir. In TCP mode pod-spec stamps `AX_PROXY_CA_PEM=<pem>` + points cert vars at a tmpfs path (`/home/runner/.ax/proxy-ca/ca.crt`, the existing HOME emptyDir) and the RUNNER writes the PEM at boot; hostPath mode keeps the mounted `/var/run/ax/proxy-ca/ca.crt`. The runner's CA-from-env writer no-ops when the file already exists, so hostPath mode "wins when present" (card requirement) with one code path. | The card's file pointers named pod-spec.ts:327 (the `pc.endpoint` branch) + open-session.ts:506 (subprocess CA-write to mirror). The subprocess backend already writes the CA to a per-session tmpdir + points NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS/SSL_CERT_FILE/GIT_SSL_CAINFO/DENO_CERT there — k8s TCP mode is the same shape, except the CA arrives as an env var (the host can't write into the runner pod) and the runner does the write. | (a) keep CA on a hostPath even in TCP mode (rejected — GKE Sandbox bans hostPath, the whole point); (b) ship CA via a downward-API projected volume or a Secret mount (rejected — extra k8s object per session, env-var is simplest and the cert is public per I1); (c) discriminate TCP via a new explicit `mode` enum (rejected — `proxySocketHostPath` empty + endpoint set is already an unambiguous signal, no new field needed on the resolved config beyond `proxyEndpoint`). |
| 2026-06-03 | **TASK-149: add `advertisedEndpoint?` to CredentialProxyConfig (analogous to sandbox-k8s `hostIpcUrl`) so `proxy:open-session` returns the cluster Service URL, not the bind address.** `buildEndpointString` returns `tcp://<host>:<port>` where host defaults to `127.0.0.1` / the bind host — unreachable from another pod. The chart computes a `credentialProxyServiceUrl` helper (mirror of `hostIpcUrl`) and the preset threads it into the plugin as `advertisedEndpoint`. The plugin returns it verbatim (must be `tcp://...` so the orchestrator's `endpointToProxyConfig` rewrites it to `http://host:port` for HTTPS_PROXY). | The IPC listener solved the identical bind-vs-advertised problem with `hostIpcUrl` (config.ts) — copy the shape exactly. No new hook surface (open-session output `proxyEndpoint` field pre-exists; only its VALUE changes in TCP mode). | (a) have the orchestrator compute the Service URL (rejected — the proxy plugin owns the endpoint contract, one source of truth I4); (b) reuse the bind host as the advertised host (rejected — 127.0.0.1 is wrong cross-pod and 0.0.0.0 isn't a dialable address). |
| 2026-06-03 | TASK-149 Phase 5 (codex review, BOTH accepted as real bugs): **P1 — a new TCP proxy Service needs BOTH a runner-egress rule (sandbox-restrict.yaml) AND a host-INGRESS rule (agent-runtime-network.yaml) or the CNI denies the connect.** The host NetworkPolicy selects the host pod and only admitted the IPC port (8080) from runners; the proxy listens inside the SAME host pod on 8888, so without a host-ingress rule for 8888 packets are dropped before reaching the proxy container — TCP sessions boot with a correct AX_PROXY_ENDPOINT but every proxy connect fails. Fix: gate a 2nd ingress port (credentialProxy.tcp.port) into the runner→host ingress rule under `if .Values.credentialProxy.tcp.enabled`. **P2 — a TCP listen port WITHOUT an advertised endpoint silently ships an unreachable proxy** (binds 0.0.0.0, advertises tcp://0.0.0.0:<port> → http://0.0.0.0:<port>, undialable cross-pod). Fix: env loader throws when tcpPort set + advertisedEndpoint unset, AND createK8sPlugins throws the same (defense-in-depth for a hand-rolled config). | Both are reachability gaps a unit/render test caught only once written: the NetworkPolicy contract is two-sided (egress on the caller + ingress on the target) and I only wrote the egress half; the advertised endpoint was `?optional` on the config but is load-bearing in the k8s TCP posture. Regression tests added: render-test asserts the host-network NP proxy ingress port (+ its absence in hostPath mode); preset-test asserts the throw on port-without-endpoint. | (P1) put the host-ingress on the public NP instead — rejected, runners must NOT reach the public surface (issue #39); the IPC-rule's runner selector is the right place. (P2) auto-derive the advertised endpoint from the bind host — rejected, 0.0.0.0 has no derivation to a Service DNS name; the chart owns that URL (the credentialProxyAdvertisedEndpoint helper), so fail-loud on a partial config is correct. |

| 2026-06-03 | TASK-149 Phase 5 round 2 (codex, BOTH accepted): **P2a — the pod-spec TCP discriminator must key off `proxyConfig.endpoint` (set) + no hostPath, NOT a second `config.proxyEndpoint` knob.** My first cut required `config.proxyEndpoint.length>0 && proxySocketHostPath empty && pc.endpoint` — but a programmatic caller who set the proxy to TCP (so `pc.endpoint` is a URL) yet forgot `sandbox.proxyEndpoint` would get `AX_PROXY_ENDPOINT` stamped while the CA vars still pointed at the unmounted hostPath path + `AX_PROXY_CA_PEM` omitted → every TLS call fails. Fix: `tcpMode = proxySocketHostPath empty && pc.endpoint !== undefined` (the runner's ACTUAL inputs, not a lockstep config knob). `config.proxyEndpoint` survives ONLY as the config-level mutual-exclusivity gate in resolveConfig — not dead, but no longer read by pod-spec. **P2b — `printf "%s-proxy" fullname | trunc 63` truncates AFTER appending, so a 62-63-char fullnameOverride loses the suffix and the proxy Service collides with the host Service (helm refuses two Services, one name).** Fix: reserve the suffix first — `$base := fullname | trunc 57` then `printf "%s-proxy" $base | trunc 63` (the git-server-experimental helper's pattern). | The first round's discriminator coupled CA-delivery to an operator config field instead of the runner's actual env; the lesson is to derive a security-relevant branch from the data the consumer truly receives. The helm-truncation bug is a known footgun the chart already solved once (gitServerExperimentalComponentName) — I should have copied that suffix-reserving form for ANY new `<name>-<suffix>` helper. Regression tests: pod-spec asserts TCP mode with config.proxyEndpoint UNSET; render asserts unique Service names + `-proxy` suffix under a 62-char fullnameOverride. | (P2a) require sandbox.proxyEndpoint whenever TCP proxy is enabled — rejected, that re-introduces the same lockstep-coupling the bug is about; deriving from pc.endpoint is the single source of truth. (P2b) shorten the suffix — rejected, `-proxy` is already minimal; reserving 6 chars of head budget is the standard fix. |

| 2026-06-03 | TASK-149 Phase 5 round 3 (codex, BOTH accepted): **P2 — a skill/connector credential slot NAMED like a proxy control var (e.g. `AX_PROXY_CA_PEM`) lands in `pc.envMap`, which pod-spec appended LAST, so the kubelet's last-duplicate-wins rule lets the `ax-cred:<hex>` placeholder shadow the real control value** → runner writes `ax-cred:...` as the CA file → all proxied TLS fails. Fix: build a `reservedProxyEnv` Set from the already-stamped proxy control vars and SKIP any envMap key that collides (control wins over slot env — TASK-86 trusted-base-wins precedent). This also closes the same latent collision for AX_PROXY_ENDPOINT/UNIX_SOCKET/TOKEN/cert vars in BOTH transports. **P3 — the tcpPort-without-advertisedEndpoint guard checked `=== undefined` but not `=== ''`**, so a hand-rolled config with `advertisedEndpoint: ''` slipped through and advertised the bind address. Fix: normalize empty→undefined before the guard + before building the listen config. | The envMap-last ordering is the documented "per-session credentials win over ordinary env" rule — correct for credential placeholders, WRONG for trusted control vars the host stamps; the reserved-set is the minimal fix that keeps credential precedence for everything except the control names. Empty-string-as-present is a recurring config-validation footgun (the codebase uses `!== '' && !== undefined` everywhere for exactly this). Regression tests: pod-spec asserts a colliding AX_PROXY_CA_PEM slot can't shadow the real PEM (single entry, real value); preset asserts createK8sPlugins throws on both missing AND empty advertisedEndpoint. | (P2) reserve only AX_PROXY_CA_PEM — rejected, the same shadowing hits every control var, so reserve the whole stamped set. (P3) trust the env loader to never emit '' — rejected, createK8sPlugins is a public entry a hand-rolled config reaches directly; defense-in-depth normalizes there too. |

| 2026-06-03 | TASK-149 Phase 5 round 4 (codex P1 — REJECTED as a blocker, tracked as a follow-up; NOT silently dismissed): codex flagged that opening the proxy cluster-wide in TCP mode lets a compromised runner in session A reach a host that only session B allowlisted (and get B's ax-cred placeholders substituted), because `findAllowingSession` ORs the allowlist across ALL sessions and `Proxy-Authorization` is attribution-only. **This is a REAL property but it is PRE-EXISTING, not a regression introduced by TASK-149:** (1) listener.ts:52 documents "the allowlist check ORs across all registered sessions" — identical in hostPath/kind mode, where every runner pod already reaches the same shared socket; (2) decisions.md TASK-52 (2026-05-26) records that per-session egress ISOLATION "was considered and REJECTED as out-of-scope — it would change the allow/deny gate (regression risk on the egress path)". My change is TRANSPORT-ONLY and keeps `findAllowingSession` UNTOUCHED (the card's "Keep I1/I5 untouched" + "S1 has no code-level dependents"). Per-session proxy authorization is a separate, larger architectural decision that touches the security-critical egress gate — exactly the blast radius this card forbids. Disposition: ship TASK-149 (transport migration, legacy path unchanged, acceptance met), surface per-session-isolation as a deferred follow-up card + flag it in the PR security note. | The card scope is explicit (transport + CA delivery; no gate change), and the cross-session OR is a documented, deliberately-deferred design — redesigning it inside a transport-migration PR would be scope creep AND would re-open the exact egress-gate regression risk TASK-52 avoided. This is the "accept minor/out-of-scope review issues as non-blocking + track them" pattern, not a silent dismissal. | (a) add per-session token authz to findAllowingSession in THIS PR — rejected: changes the allow/deny gate (TASK-52's explicit no-go), out of card scope, large blast radius; (b) per-session listener-per-pod isolation — rejected: a much bigger architecture change (N listeners or a sidecar), its own design; (c) ignore it — rejected: it's a real production-multi-tenant gap worth a tracked card, just not a blocker for the transport migration. |

## 2026-06-07 — TASK-168: BackendConfig (SSE timeout) into the chart

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Decision | Template the GKE `BackendConfig` (timeoutSec, default 3600) + the host Service `cloud.google.com/backend-config` annotation into the chart, gated behind a new `ingress.backendConfig.enabled` flag (default off). |
| Rationale | Today it's a hand-applied `kubectl` step (GKE.md M7); a `helm upgrade` re-renders the host Service and drops the annotation → SSE timeout silently reverts to the GCE LB default 30s and chat streams cut mid-answer. Putting both objects in the chart makes them survive upgrades. |
| Alternatives | (a) Keep it manual (rejected — the whole bug is that manual annotations don't survive upgrades). (b) Always render the BackendConfig (rejected — `cloud.google.com/v1` is a GKE-only CRD; kind has no such type, so an unconditional render breaks the kind path / non-GKE backends). Hence the `enabled` gate, default off, turned on only in gke-values.yaml — same posture as `ingress.enabled` and `networkPolicies.lbHealthCheckCidrs`. |
| Shape | New `templates/host/backendconfig.yaml` (renders iff `ingress.backendConfig.enabled`); conditional `annotations` block on `templates/host/service.yaml`; new `ax-next.backendConfigName` helper (`<host-component-name>-bc`, truncation-safe); values `ingress.backendConfig.{enabled:false, timeoutSec:3600}`; gke-values.yaml flips `enabled:true`. Annotation value is the JSON `{"default":"<bc-name>"}` GKE expects. |
| GKE.md | Step M7 simplified from a kubectl step to a values note (`ingress.backendConfig.enabled=true`, configurable `timeoutSec`); the "applied via kubectl, drops on helm upgrade" caveat removed; migration-table "(new — Step M7)" reference updated to point at the chart value. |

## 2026-06-08 — TASK-187 Skill-reflection recurrence via consolidated source_observations (b′), not transcripts

| 2026-06-08 | The durable per-conversation key is `AgentContext.conversationId`, NOT `ctx.sessionId`. The card asked to "confirm sessionId is stable across a conversation's turns" — it is NOT: the J6 routed path lets two concurrent agent:invokes for the same conversation SHARE a sessionId (orchestrator.ts ~864), and `Conversation.activeSessionId` is nullable + re-bound across turns/respawns (conversations/types.ts). So recurrence is keyed on `conversationId`. This is the "key on THAT instead — do not guess" branch, NOT a `blocked` design gap (conversationId exists on the same ctx). | sessionId is neither one-per-conversation nor stable; conversationId is the conversation's identity. | key on sessionId (per card hint) → would mis-count (a multi-invoke conversation looks like several) and miss respawn continuity. |
| 2026-06-08 | Recurrence gate = ≥2 DISTINCT conversation ids, materialized on the DOC frontmatter as `source_conversations: string[]` (deduped, first-seen order). NOT `source_observations.length>=2` (the observer fires per-message, so one conversation yields ≥N obs → a naive length gate crystallizes a one-off). | The inbox obs carrying each `conversation_id` is DELETED on promote (I12), so the doc is the ONLY surviving home for the signal; the reflection turn reads it straight from `/agent/memory/docs/…` — no transcript-read surface (point of b′; TASK-67 gitignore intact). | resolve obs-id→conv-id at reflection time → impossible, inbox files are gone. |

A recurring procedure's 2nd occurrence is almost always a near-duplicate summary → Jaccard dedup hit → previously the conv-id was dropped and recurrence stalled at 1. | This is exactly the recurrence case; dropping it makes the POSITIVE walk fail. mergeConversationIntoDoc is a no-op (no rewrite) for an already-seen/undefined conv. | only count conv-ids on append/write → false-negative for near-dup recurrence. |

## 2026-07-01 — memory_search snippets: postgres tsquery parity (feat/memory-search-snippets)

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-01 | Postgres `memory:index:search` builds its tsquery as OR-joined, per-token double-quoted phrases fed to `websearch_to_tsquery` (`buildOrTsQuery`), replacing the plan's literal `plainto_tsquery`. Applied uniformly to WHERE / `ts_rank` / `ts_headline`. | `plainto_tsquery` ANDs terms; sqlite's `escapeFts5Query` has always OR-joined quoted tokens. The shared conformance kit (Tests 8b/8c) now enforces parity: multi-term query must hit a doc containing only one term, and operator-shaped tokens (`-foo`, embedded `"`) must be neutralized, never inverted into NOT-matching. Quoting each token is what neutralizes `websearch_to_tsquery`'s `-`/`"` operators (mirror of sqlite's quoting). | Keep `plainto_tsquery` → deterministically fails the kit's body-only-value case (AND semantics); raw unquoted OR join → `foo -bar` becomes `foo \| !bar`, matching everything *lacking* bar. |
| 2026-07-01 | `RetrievalResult.snippet` is REQUIRED, so orchestrator map-`<load>` rows set `snippet: ''` (empty ≠ "excerpt == summary"); consumers must skip rendering empty snippets (bench `formatSearchResults` omits the `match:` line when `snippet.trim()===''`). | `<load>` rows have no query-matched excerpt (map densification is design follow-up #2). Rendering `match: ""` reads as "matched nothing" on exactly the rows the orchestrator ranked highest — would suppress the orchestrator lift in the e2e eval. | Optional field → half-wired contract; summary duplicated into snippet → callers can't tell "no excerpt" apart. |

| Date | Decision | Rationale | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-01 | Use **quoted** empty selectors `StartSel="", StopSel=""`, NOT the design-doc §3 literal `StartSel=, StopSel=`. VERIFIED against a real postgres:16-alpine container: the unquoted trailing-empty form throws `ERROR: invalid parameter list format`, and a bare `StartSel=` grabs the next comma as its value (yields a `,graduated,` artifact). The quoted form parses and yields TRULY empty markers. | The design doc's literal shape does not parse on pg16 — this is exactly why PR #375 shipped the `<b>`+`.replace(/<\/?b>/g,'')` workaround instead of empty selectors. Quoting is the documented way to pass an empty option value. | design-doc literal `StartSel=, StopSel=` → runtime error; reorder so a non-empty option trails the empties → parses but fragile/opaque. |
| 2026-07-01 | Delete the mapper regex `String(r.snippet).replace(/<\/?b>/g,'')`; map `snippet: r.snippet` directly (mirrors sqlite). | With empty selectors ts_headline emits NO highlight markers, so the regex is dead. The task's premise ("the regex also eats a literal `<b>` in body text") is FALSE on postgres: ts_headline's default parser classifies `<b>` as a `tag` token and DROPS it from windowed output *before* the mapper runs (verified — `HighlightAll=true` is the only mode that preserves tags, but it returns the whole body, defeating a bounded snippet). So the regex only ever stripped ts_headline's OWN markers; removing it + empty selectors is a clean equivalent. | keep the regex → dead code once selectors are empty. |
| 2026-07-01 | **Literal `<b>` does NOT survive on postgres** (ts_headline tag-stripping), so the "new test for literal `<b>` surviving" acceptance is split by backend: SQLITE unit test asserts `<b>` survives verbatim (true — FTS5 `snippet()` returns raw original text); POSTGRES unit test asserts the snippet is CLEAN (no `<b>`/`</b>`, surrounding words preserved) and documents the divergence. Did NOT add a sentinel-escape hack to force `<b>` through ts_headline. NOTE (reviewer finding 1): the drop is BROADER than `<b>` — ts_headline omits ANY `<word>`/`</word>`/`<word/>` token (`<Button>`, `<div>`, TS/Java generics `List<String>`); a bare `a < b` / `Map<Integer,Value>` survives. Not rare in a coding-assistant's own memory, but it's PRE-EXISTING ts_headline behaviour (windowed headline always tag-drops, independent of the selector change) and the snippet is an explicitly lossy hint (`memory_read_section` is the full-fidelity fallback). Comment in queries.ts + this row broadened for honesty. | Parity target is "match sqlite behaviour", but ts_headline fundamentally can't preserve tag tokens in a windowed snippet; a `<`→sentinel→`<` transform is fragile, adds an untrusted-content transform layer over the agent's OWN content (YAGNI, minimize-capabilities). | sentinel-escape to preserve tags → rejected (fragile, over-engineered for a corner case); block on the mismatch → rejected (resolvable technically, not human-owned). |
| 2026-07-01 | Reviewer nits handled: added a topK-cap + score-descending test (finding 2 — the outer-select refactor's "same rows, same order" contract was otherwise unpinned; every other test seeded ≤ topK docs and used order-independent `findIndex`); corrected stale `plainto_tsquery` comments in plugin.ts + plugin.test.ts (finding 4 — backend uses `websearch_to_tsquery`). REJECTED finding 3 (restore `String(r.snippet)`): kept `snippet: r.snippet` — `body` is `TEXT NOT NULL` so ts_headline always returns a string, the return schema is `z.string()`, and bare `r.snippet` matches sqlite's mapper (parity). | ax-code-reviewer APPROVE; findings all Minor/Nit. | — |
| 2026-07-01 | `…` truncation-marker parity via `MaxFragments=2, FragmentDelimiter=…`. Final options: `MaxWords=48, MinWords=16, MaxFragments=2, FragmentDelimiter=…, StartSel="", StopSel=""`. `…` appears BETWEEN disjoint match windows on long/scattered docs; single-match + short bodies stay one window with no `…` (8b stays green, verified). Documented residual: ts_headline emits NO leading/trailing boundary `…` (sqlite marks single-window boundary truncation; postgres can't). | This is the only way ts_headline emits `…`: with `MaxFragments=1` the delimiter is inert. MaxFragments=2 keeps the common single-match case identical (~48-word window) while giving the reviewer's requested `…` where content is elided between matches. | MaxFragments=1 + FragmentDelimiter → delimiter never fires (no `…`); app-layer boundary `…` via body prefix/suffix compare → unreliable (ts_headline normalizes whitespace + drops tags, so no byte-exact substring). |

Behaviour-preserving (same rows, same order). | keep ts_headline inline in the flat SELECT → parses body for every WHERE match. |
