## 2026-08-24 — TASK-321: the postgres tag stays duplicated at 115 call sites (ANALYSED-NOT-BUILT)

The bump procedure, so the next bumper does not re-derive it. Two edits, not 116:

```sh
git grep -lE 'postgres:16-alpine' -- packages presets | grep -v '\.json$' \
  | xargs sed -i '' 's/postgres:16-alpine/postgres:17-alpine/g'
```

then hand-edit the CI pull list at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:110` (`images=(postgres:16-alpine)`).
The `git grep -l` half was run on this branch and matches exactly 115 files, all `.ts`.
(`sed -i ''` is the BSD/macOS spelling; GNU sed wants a bare `-i`.) The `grep -v '\.json$'`
is load-bearing and mirrors what the guard does: `packages/memory-strata/test/bench/internal-corpus.json`
is a benchmark corpus whose *document text* quotes testcontainers code, so the three
`new PostgreSqlContainer(...)` spellings it contains (out of four `postgres:16-alpine`
occurrences in that one file) are data, not call sites.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Close as analysed-not-built.** No `POSTGRES_IMAGE` constant, no guard change, no new package. The literals stay. |
| **Rationale** | The counts were re-measured on this branch and the card was right, exactly: **115** `new PostgreSqlContainer('postgres:16-alpine')` call sites, in 115 distinct `.ts` files, across 21 workspace projects — plus the one CI pull-list entry, for 116 live copies. Repo-wide the tag string appears 155 times across 132 files (`git grep -o 'postgres:16-alpine' -- ':!.claude/memory'`), so the other 39 are inert (fixtures, the guard's own self-tests, docs). **The `':!.claude/memory'` exclusion is not cosmetic and is its own small lesson:** writing this row *raised* the unscoped repo-wide total, because the row quotes the tag — a whole-repo count is not a stable fact once memory prose starts citing it, which is the same trap as citing a line number. Prefer the scoped command above. And postgres is the only image the repo actually starts: outside the benchmark corpus noted above, the only other container constructors in the tree are the guard's own self-test strings. Per the epic's own measurement pass (not re-audited here), **this is the first card in it whose numbers survived measurement**, against 7 of the previous 8 that did not — worth recording because this epic has so far written down only the failures, which skews how much a card is trusted. The duplication is nonetheless not worth abstracting, because **a shared constant does not reduce the bump to fewer edits — it is two either way — and the guard pays for it** (see the next two rows). |
| **Alternatives** | Both rejected — see below. |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Rejected alternative A — `POSTGRES_IMAGE` exported from `@ax/test-harness`. Rejected on cost, NOT on Invariant 2 — and the card's Invariant-2 claim is FALSE.** |
| **Rationale** | The card asserted that "115 call sites spread over 21 packages cannot all import from one plugin" because of Invariant 2 (no cross-plugin imports). That premise is unfounded and is corrected here so nobody re-files this card on it: `eslint.config.mjs` explicitly whitelists `'!@ax/test-harness'`, 114 of the 115 call-site files **already import from it** (the lone holdout is `presets/k8s/src/__tests__/prod-bootstrap.test.ts`), and 116 files under `packages/` and `presets/` already reference its `stopPostgresContainer` — 114 of them callers, the other two being the definition in `packages/test-harness/src/stop-postgres-container.ts` and the barrel re-export in `packages/test-harness/src/index.ts` (and repo-wide the name also appears in docs and memory prose, so scope the grep or the number looks larger still). A constant in `packages/test-harness/src/index.ts` is architecturally **legal** and needs no new package. What kills it is **cost, and specifically that the abstraction buys nothing at bump time.** Today a bump is two edits: one `sed` over the 115 files, plus the CI pull list. With a constant it is still two edits: the declaration, plus the CI pull list. Identical — and in exchange the guard grows three permanent mechanisms. **Be precise about which three, because the first draft of this row was not.** `scripts/__tests__/ci-prepull-covers-test-images.test.js` walks every `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs` file under `SOURCE_ROOTS = ['packages', 'presets']` as **text**, and `packages/test-harness/src/index.ts` is inside that corpus — so the guard would **not** need import resolution, monorepo path mapping, or re-export chasing. (This row originally claimed it would. That was an overstatement, caught in review, and it is worth leaving the correction visible: overstating a mechanism to strengthen an argument is the exact defect this epic exists to stop, and it is easiest to commit in the sentence you most want to be true.) What it really needs is: a regex reading the tag off the declaration so the scanned set still contains a literal; an exemption so `NON_LITERAL_CONSTRUCTOR` stops hard-failing on `new PostgreSqlContainer(POSTGRES_IMAGE)`; and named-constructor usages counted as `sites` so the `sites.length > 50` / `projects.size > 10` floors stay meaningful. **And separate the two costs, because the first draft ran them together.** The cheap guard above is cheap to *build*; what it cannot do is verify the **binding** — that the `POSTGRES_IMAGE` each call site names is the canonical one and not a shadowed local constant. Only a real resolver closes that, and *that* is the expensive option. So the choice is (cheap whitelist + definition scan, one bounded blind spot) XOR (resolver, no blind spot, expensive). Today's guard has **neither** — every argument is a literal it reads directly, so there is no binding to verify and nothing to trust. Declining both is therefore declining a real erosion of a zero-trust total scan, not dodging implementation heft. Paying that, plus editing all 115 files, plus keeping the CI edit anyway, **to save nothing on the bump**, is a bad trade. Note the shape of the correction, because it is the more useful half: the overstated version was not just wrong, it was *fragile* — a reader who discovered the resolver is cheap would conclude the objection had evaporated and re-file the card, when the real objection (the blind spot) still holds. (Coverage note for the next reader: every repo path cited in this section is rooted and therefore checked by `scripts/__tests__/memory-cited-paths-exist.test.js` — **except `eslint.config.mjs`**. That guard's `PATH_TOKEN` needs at least one slash, so a **repo-root** file can never be a rooted citation and is structurally invisible to it. Nothing is wrong with the citation; the guard simply cannot see it, which is the kind of thing this epic has decided to say out loud rather than let a green run imply.) |
| **Alternatives** | Teach the guard to resolve the constant first, then migrate (the card's own ordering) — rejected for the same reason: the ordering is correct, but it is the resolver itself that is the cost. |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Rejected alternative B — a new shared pure-data package holding the tag.** And: **the guard's set-equality is what makes the duplication survivable, and must not be weakened.** |
| **Rationale** | B is unnecessary (A shows `@ax/test-harness` is already reachable) and precedent-rejected: the TASK-245 human ruling turned down "a new shared pure-data package" as *a package for four strings*. One string is not a better case. As for why living with the duplication is safe — it is guarded, not latent. The guard asserts **set equality** between the tags it scans out of the sources and the CI pull list, so a partial bump reddens in **either** direction: miss a call site and the scanned set has two tags, which a one-entry pull list satisfies neither way; miss the pull list and it reddens too. Anti-vacuity floors (`sites.length > 50`, `projects.size > 10`) stop the scan passing on an empty parse. So the duplication is mechanical and about one command per bump, and the thing that must never be traded away is that set-equality assertion. |
| **Alternatives** | Do the refactor anyway to "close the card properly" — rejected; forcing an abstraction to justify a card is the failure mode the card body itself warned about. |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **TASK-321 process note: the `ax-code-reviewer` was run on a prose-only diff (not the docs-only skip), and BOTH dispatches stalled at delivery — findings were recovered only by reading their emitted messages.** |
| **Rationale** | Same call as TASK-320: on a card whose deliverable *is* a set of factual sentences, the reviewer is the only gate that can fail it, and it earned its keep — it caught **three** counting errors that every automated gate passed. All three were the same species: a number measured in one scope and stated in another. (a) The repo-wide occurrence total was **self-inflating**, because the analysis row quotes the tag it counts — writing the sentence changed the number, which is the counting equivalent of citing a line number. (b) The benchmark corpus's four tag occurrences were conflated with its three `new PostgreSqlContainer(...)` spellings. (c) A `stopPostgresContainer` count scoped to `packages/` + `presets/` was stated unscoped, where docs and memory prose push it higher. **Generalisation worth keeping: a count in memory prose must carry the scope that produced it, and any count that includes `.claude/memory/` is unstable by construction.** | 
| **Alternatives** | Take yolo-ship's docs-only skip (rejected — nothing else reads prose for truth); state the counts unscoped and let the reader re-derive (rejected — that is how all three errors arose). |

A reviewer dispatch from inside an isolated worktree should say so up front — the second dispatch did, and got measurably further. |

The id remains on the fire row. | Leave it on the wire as dead weight (rejected — an unread field invites a subscriber to key off it, which is the exact boundary-review hazard). Add the link to justify keeping it (rejected — overturning Phase D is a human's call and a wider diff). |
| 2026-08-24 | **TASK-313: the schema strip guard asserts BOTH removed fields, not just the one the card started with.** `'fireId' in parsed === false` AND `'conversationId' in parsed === false`, in `packages/routines/src/__tests__/return-schemas.test.ts`. | That single case is the load-bearing one in the file. A field re-added to the handler but NOT the schema is stripped silently by `z.object` and fails nothing; a field re-added to BOTH would sail past every other assertion, because the round-trip cases only ever feed the schema shapes it already accepts. Feeding it a payload containing both removed fields is the only assertion that catches either. Verified by re-adding `conversationId` to the schema: the guard reddened for the right reason (field retained), and the round-trip and canary cases reddened alongside it. | Drop the guard once the fields were gone (rejected — deleting the guard is what lets the leak come back). |

## 2026-08-24 — TASK-302: every container hook already has a budget; the card's premise, its counts and its acceptance criterion all fail (ANALYSED-NOT-BUILT)

All counts below were re-derived on this branch. Scopes are stated because two of them
move if you widen the scope, and one of the card's own numbers is what a wider scope
produced. The hook inventory is a paren-balanced scan of `*.ts`/`*.tsx` under `packages/`,
`presets/` and `deploy/`, classifying a hook by whether its **closing** line carries a
numeric second argument.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Close as analysed-not-built. No hook gets an explicit budget, no `vitest.config` is touched, no `packages/` source changes.** |
| **Rationale** | The card's scope sentence — "give the 76 unbudgeted container teardowns and the 7 unbudgeted `routines` setups an explicit budget" — rests on a premise that is false in the way that matters. **"No explicit budget" is not "unbounded", and here it is never unbounded.** vitest always applies a budget: `hookTimeout` defaults to `10000` and `testTimeout` to `5000` (both read out of the installed vitest 4.1.5 itself — its bundled CLI-option help text and the `@default` tags on `testTimeout`/`hookTimeout` in its shipped type declarations — rather than from documentation. Deliberately described rather than cited by path: those files live under `node_modules/`, which `scripts/__tests__/memory-cited-paths-exist.test.js` does not resolve, so a path here would look checked and not be). So the real inventory is: **113** container-start `beforeAll` hooks, of which **11** carry no explicit second argument — and every one of those 11 lives in a package whose `vitest.config.ts` sets `hookTimeout: 60_000`, so **not a single container start in the repo runs at the 10s default**. On the teardown side, **103** container-stop `afterAll` hooks under `packages/` carry no explicit argument: **73** sit in packages with no `hookTimeout` override (10s) and **30** inherit a package-level 60s/120s config. Zero of the 216 are unbounded. Separately, **it does not bite in CI**: across the last 100 push-to-main runs of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, 11 failed, and **not one of their failed-step logs (`gh run view --log-failed`) contains `Hook timed out`** — in any package, at any budget. (The one full run log pulled for timing, at the base commit, also contains zero.) The two that contain a timeout at all match `Test timed out in 5000ms` exactly, i.e. the default *testTimeout*, and the most recent of them is `packages/test-harness/src/__tests__/stub-runner.test.ts` at 5550ms — a package that starts **no** postgres container. The shape CI actually shows is not the shape this card is about. |
| **Alternatives** | Apply the card's 30s budget to all 103 teardowns (rejected — see the next row; the criterion is self-contradictory). Apply 60s to the 73 at the default and leave the 30 alone (rejected here on scope, not on merit — that IS the defensible change, it is the timeout pattern that already exists in-tree, and it is being filed as its own card so it gets its own review; doing it inside a card whose stated premise is false would launder the premise). Re-file the card with corrected counts (rejected — the corrected counts are what closes it). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **The card's acceptance criterion cannot be satisfied, and that is the finding — not a detail to work around.** |
| **Rationale** | The card asks for "an explicit budget, 30s not 120s, so a real hang must still fail rather than stall the suite", plus "every container-start and container-stop hook carries an explicit budget". Applied to the measured tree, one number moves the two halves in **opposite** directions: the 73 teardowns currently at the 10s default get **loosened threefold**, making the suite *more* tolerant of exactly the hang the card exists to catch, while the 30 teardowns currently inheriting 60s/120s get **tightened**. It is a 103-file diff that is wrong in both directions at once. Sharper still: all **73** of the 10s-default teardowns sit in a file whose *own* container-start `beforeAll` declares **120_000** (59 files) or **60_000** (14 files) for the same container's lifecycle — so a flat 30s would also contradict the budget its own file already declares two lines above. There is no single number that satisfies the criterion as written. |
| **Alternatives** | Pick 30s anyway and note the regression (rejected — shipping a knowingly loosening change to 73 hooks to satisfy a sentence). Split into two numbers (rejected — that is no longer this card, and it is the follow-up card's job). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **The card's "seven unbudgeted `routines` setups" is a phantom, and so is its "routines 3" teardown row. `packages/routines` has ZERO unbudgeted container hooks in either direction.** |
| **Rationale** | All **10** container-start `beforeAll`s in `packages/routines/src/__tests__/` close with `}, 120_000)` and all **10** container-stop `afterAll`s close with `}, 60_000)` — checked on this branch and at the commit the card measured. The earlier pass matched the `beforeAll(` **opening** line, where the timeout cannot appear, and concluded absence. **Transferable, and the reason this row exists: a vitest hook's budget is the last argument, so grep the CLOSING line of a hook, never the opening one — an opening-line scan reports "no budget" for every hook in the repo that has one.** This is also why the card's teardown total (76) and this measurement's (103) diverge in *both* directions: the card missed the ~30 teardowns in packages whose budget is config-level, and invented 3 in `routines`. |
| **Alternatives** | Record only the corrected total (rejected — the total is not the lesson; the grep is). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Correct the card's TRAP: `stopPostgresContainer` does NOT suppress the symptom of a hung or failing `stop()`. It is not a silent-failure defect and needs no narrowing.** |
| **Rationale** | The card warns that raising a stop budget means "a genuinely hung `stop()` now hangs *longer* inside a handler that suppresses its only symptom", and asks whether the suppression should be narrowed. Read against `packages/test-harness/src/stop-postgres-container.ts`, that is wrong on the mechanism. The helper installs `process.on('uncaughtException')` / `('unhandledRejection')` listeners that return early **only** for the benign `57P01` admin-shutdown shape and otherwise detach themselves and **re-emit** the error; `await container.stop()` is **not** inside a `catch`, so a *rejecting* stop propagates and reds the suite exactly as it would without the helper, and a *hung* stop produces a hook timeout that a `process`-level exception listener cannot intercept at all. The guard is armed for the duration of `stop()` plus one macrotask and is removed in a `finally`. So the premise that raising the budget lengthens a window in which the failure is invisible does not hold — the window suppresses a racing **pool's** shutdown error, not the stop's own outcome. One genuine residual, small enough to record rather than card: `isBenignAdminShutdown` returns true on the message substring **regardless of `code`**, so an unrelated error whose message quotes `terminating connection due to administrator command` would also be swallowed — within that same sub-second window, on a string no product code emits. |
| **Alternatives** | Narrow the predicate to `code === '57P01'` only (rejected — not in a prose-only PR, and the substring arm is deliberate: the same error arrives without a `code` on some socket paths, which is the case the original helper was written for). Leave the card's claim standing (rejected — it is the kind of claim that gets re-filed as a security-flavoured card by the next reader). |

## 2026-08-24 — TASK-318: the concurrency bound is REAL and undocumented, and BOTH cost estimates were wrong (ANALYSED-NOT-BUILT)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Close as analysed-not-built. No `maxConcurrency`, no root vitest project, no CI shard.** But **write down the bound**, because "there is no bound anywhere" is the part of the card that is false. |
| **Rationale** | The bound exists; it is simply nowhere written down. `pnpm`'s `--workspace-concurrency` defaults to **4** (read off `pnpm recursive run --help` on the pinned pnpm 10.33.2, not from docs), and vitest's run-mode worker default is `Math.max(numCpus - 1, 1)` — `getDefaultThreadsCount` in the installed vitest 4.1.5 — which is **3** on a 4-vCPU GitHub runner. Four package lanes × three file workers is a hard structural ceiling of **12** concurrent test files, and since each container-starting file starts **at most one** container — in a `beforeAll` in 113 of the 115 such files, and via a memoized lazy helper in the other two (`presets/k8s/src/__tests__/prod-bootstrap.test.ts` and `presets/k8s/src/__tests__/acceptance.test.ts`, whose `ensurePostgresStarted()` is called from `it()` blocks) — that ceiling bounds the container count too. The card's "~12 concurrent postgres containers" is therefore right as arithmetic and wrong as a diagnosis: nothing is unbounded, so a bound is not a missing safety property, it is a *tuning* change. And the card's own sweeping inventory has one hole — `presets/k8s/vitest.config.k8s-e2e.ts` **does** set `fileParallelism: false`. It is reached only by that package's `test:k8s-e2e` script and never by `pnpm -r run test`, so the claim is materially true for the default path and literally false about the tree; more usefully, it means an in-tree precedent for serialising already exists and can be pointed at. |
| **Alternatives** | Set `maxConcurrency` / a root vitest project (rejected — costs CI time, see the next row, and fixes none of the observed shapes). Shard CI (rejected — same cost argument plus a new mechanism to maintain, for a failure class CI has not shown). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Both prior cost estimates are wrong, and the reason they are wrong is the same one. Measured: serialising files within the container projects costs ≈ +9 min, not "+15 min" (TASK-302's trap) and not "+4–8 min" (the reconciliation handed to this PR).** |
| **Rationale** | **Every figure in this row is re-derivable from named GitHub Actions runs, and should be re-derived rather than trusted — the reviewer on this PR verified the whole structural layer but explicitly did not reach the CI layer.** The base-commit run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is **32767256696** (`main` @ `2216a989`); the two failures carrying a timeout are **32759209871** and **32412449799**; the job-duration sample is the 12 most recent push-to-main runs as of 2026-08-24. Measured from run 32767256696: the `Test (full suite)` step took **8:13** of wall clock, while the 78 per-project vitest `Duration` lines in that same step sum to **19.0 min**. That is a **realised end-to-end parallelism of 2.32×** — not vitest's 12, and not even pnpm's 4. `pnpm -r run test` walks the dependency topology, so lanes idle waiting on the long poles, and the 21 postgres-starting projects are **75%** of all project time (859s of 1141s). Both estimates missed this same fact from opposite sides: "+15 min" assumed near-total serialisation of 113 container starts against a baseline it treated as fully parallel; "+4–8 min" assumed pnpm's 4 lanes stay *saturated*, which they measurably do not. Modelling `fileParallelism:false` per project as `import + tests + setup` (vitest prints those as sums across files) against the observed 2.32×: **≈ +8.9 min** for the 21 container projects, **≈ +10.5 min** repo-wide — roughly a doubling of the step. Useful hard ceiling for anyone re-litigating this: one project at a time with files still parallel inside is bounded by the 19.0 min sum, i.e. **+10.8 min**, so no lane-preserving serialisation strategy can reach "+15 min". Baseline for comparison: the push-to-main `test` **job** ran a median of **9:14** (range 7:18–9:51) over the 11 successful runs in the last 12, and it is unambiguously the long pole — 9:25 against 3:43 for the next-longest job in the base run. |
| **Alternatives** | Repeat the "+4–8 min" figure I was handed (rejected — it is an estimate, and this is a measurement that contradicts it). Quote a PR-run baseline too (rejected — the PR `test` job is affected-package-scoped, so its duration tracks the diff rather than the suite: 1:12 to 5:16 across the last 7 PR runs. **A median over that is not a baseline and should not be cited as one.**). Actually run the serialised suite to replace the model with a measurement (rejected for this prose-only PR, and noted as the honest gap: the +8.9 is derived from one run's own printed per-file sums, not from a serialised run). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **The mask-vs-fix disagreement, resolved: raising a teardown budget to match the start budget in the same file is a FIX, not a mask — but it is a fix for a shape CI has never shown, and the reconciliation's third leg does not survive.** |
| **Rationale** | TASK-302's pass called a timeout bump a pure mask; TASK-318's pass called it the proven in-tree remedy. Both are partly right, and the tree settles it. **Fix, for the teardown gap:** a budget too small for legitimate work is itself the defect, and the file says so in its own voice — all 73 of the 10s-default teardowns sit beside a container-start `beforeAll` in the same file declaring 60s or 120s for the same container. Nobody chose 10s for those; they inherited it. Making the pair consistent removes an oversight, and the precedent is real — `packages/agents/vitest.config.ts` names "the Hook timed out in 10000ms flake" in its own comment, and **8 of the 21** postgres-starting workspace projects now carry a `hookTimeout` override while **13** do not. **Mask, for anything else:** a bump does nothing for the third failure shape (next row), and it is not a remedy for contention, only for mis-sized budgets. **And the third leg of the reconciliation I was handed is false:** the `57P01` swallow is not "hiding the only symptom this class produces" — see the TASK-302 section above. So the honest synthesis is **two shapes, not three**: budgets address the hook-timeout shape, the fixed-iteration poll needs a real wait-for-condition, and the `57P01` handler is not a defect at all. Kept prominent because it is the load-bearing caveat: **CI shows neither shape.** Zero `Hook timed out` across 11 failures in 100 push-to-main runs; `packages/auth-better` ran 13/13 files green in 66.6s in the base run. The teardown-budget work is closing a latent gap, and its PR must say so rather than claim a flake fix. |
| **Alternatives** | Rule "mask" and drop it (rejected — contradicted by the same-file start budgets and by an in-tree precedent that names the flake). Rule "proven remedy" and build it here (rejected — "proven" overstates it; no CI failure of that shape exists to have been cured, and the change deserves its own review). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Record the fourth failure shape the card asked for: a fixed-iteration poll converts a SLOWNESS problem into an ASSERTION failure, and no timeout setting touches it.** |
| **Rationale** | `packages/auth-better/src/__tests__/init-awaits-adapter.test.ts` waits for better-auth's adapter-init with `for (let i = 0; i < 200 && contexts.length === 0; i++) await sleep(10)` and then asserts `expect(contexts).toHaveLength(1)`. That is a fixed ~2s ceiling on real migration + `loadProviders` work against a live postgres. Under contention the work overruns 2s, the loop exits, and the suite reds with a **failed assertion and zero product race** — while `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout` and any concurrency bound leave the 2s budget exactly where it is. This is the specific carve-out the card asked to be written down, and it is a genuine exception to two rules already in this repo's memory: the "assertion failure = real product race / zero-assertion crash = infra" heuristic, and the TASK-317 taxonomy's observation that all three container-flake shapes present as zero-assertion Failed Suites. This one presents as neither. The durable remedy is a time-based wait-for-condition with a generous ceiling, so contention shows up as *slow* rather than as *wrong* — filed as a follow-up, not built here. |
| **Alternatives** | Fold it into the concurrency card (rejected — bounding concurrency only makes the overrun rarer; the poll is still a 2s ceiling on unbounded work). Raise 200 to 2000 (rejected — same defect with a bigger number, and it silently doubles the failure's detection time). |

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | **Never quote a container count from a local run without stating the Ryuk state — a local count is roughly DOUBLE the CI one, so the two are not comparable.** |
| **Rationale** | This is the comparability *rule* that the TASK-317 rows above establish the mechanism for but stop short of stating. Those rows record that testcontainers starts a second container — the Ryuk reaper — on every `.start()`, and that CI disables it. The consequence for measurement is the part that keeps getting lost: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED: 'true'` on the `test` job and **nothing sets it locally**, so a developer reproducing "~12 concurrent postgres" locally is running roughly **twice** the container count CI does. It is why the local `auth-better` teardown failures two builders reported this session are load-dependent and local-only while CI shows none of them — and why a local repro is evidence about a *different*, heavier workload than the one the card is arguing about. (The sibling fact this row originally carried — that `pnpm -r run test` is fail-fast — was dropped: `mistakes.md` already says it, and two rows saying one thing in different words is its own rot.) |
| **Alternatives** | Leave it in the card bodies (rejected — both cards are closing and the rule outlives them). Fold it into the TASK-317 rows (rejected — those are a shipped PR's record; this is a measurement rule derived from them, and editing a merged card's row to carry a later card's conclusion is the in-place edit this session has been careful to avoid). |
